methodologyNotes: Granularity: Article VI is enumerated at the LETTERED sub-basket/exception level (each of 6.01(a)-(q), 6.02(a)-(p), 6.03(a)-(g), 6.04(a)-(r), 6.05(a)-(k), 6.08(a)(i)-(v) and 6.08(b)(i)-(iv), 6.09(a)-(g), 6.10 provisos (i)-(v), and 6.12(a)/(b) plus the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment is its own unit), and Article VII is enumerated at the lettered Event-of-Default clause level; Articles III, IV, V and IX-XII are at the section (or, for Section 4.01, the lettered condition) level; Article I itemizes only definitions that are load-bearing for covenants, baskets, ratios or entity scope and groups ordinary/administrative, benchmark-rate and tax definitions into single summary units; Articles VIII and IX carry BOILERPLATE_SUMMARY units for genuinely mechanical sections so no article is silently skipped. Authored solely from the source text plus the mechanical structural index.

units.description: Five-category pricing grid keyed to Total Net Leverage Ratio: Category 1 (>3.75x) ABR/Canadian Prime +1.75%, Term Benchmark/CDOR/RFR +2.75%, commitment and ticking fee 0.35%; stepping down to Category 5 (<=1.50x) at +0.00%/+1.00%/0.15%/0.15%. Category 2 applies until the first Compliance Certificate after the Effective Date; failure to deliver financials deems Category 1; incorrect financials require retroactive true-up payment.
units.notes: Pricing grid is a leverage-based ratchet; the retroactive-payment clause for misstated financials is an economic true-up, not merely mechanical.

units.description: 'Available Amount' builder basket = (i) 25% of Applicable EBITDA (pro forma) as of the most recent four-quarter period, plus (ii) net cash proceeds of Qualified Stock issuances after the Effective Date (Not Otherwise Applied, excluding Specified Equity Contributions), plus (iii) principal of Indebtedness exchanged/converted into Qualified Stock, plus (iv) Returns on Section 6.04(q) investments, plus (v) net cash proceeds from disposition of such investments/Unrestricted Subsidiaries, plus (vi) fair market value on redesignation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary as Restricted, plus (vii) Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts; minus (viii) amounts previously used under Section 6.04(q) or Section 6.08(a)(iv).
units.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: the same Available Amount is consumed by both investments under 6.04(q) and Restricted Payments under 6.08(a)(iv). Clause (i) grows with EBITDA, so basket capacity is leverage/earnings dependent.

units.description: EBITDA = Net Income plus twenty enumerated add-backs (a)(i)-(xx) (interest, taxes, D&A, losses on permitted asset sales, non-cash losses, Closing Date Transaction Expenses paid within 180 days, non-recurring/unusual expenses, run-rate Cost Savings realizable within 18 months, acquisition-related fees, transaction fees, director fees, up to $250,000 of officer board-meeting expense reimbursement, insured business interruption, amendment fees, indemnified fees, non-cash charges, Acquired EBITDA plus acquisition cost savings realizable within 12 months, integration expenses, equity-comp) minus (b)(i)-(vi) deductions (cash payments on prior non-cash charges, extraordinary gains, gains on out-of-ordinary-course dispositions, Disposed EBITDA, gains from permitted asset sales, non-cash gains).
units.notes: Load-bearing for both financial covenants, the pricing grid, Material Subsidiary, and every EBITDA-scaled basket (15%/25% of Applicable EBITDA).

units.description: 'Combined Cap': the aggregate add-backs under EBITDA clauses (a)(vii) (non-recurring/unusual expenses), (a)(viii) (run-rate Cost Savings) and (a)(xviii)(b) (Permitted Acquisition cost savings) may not exceed 20% of EBITDA calculated before such add-backs, for any four-fiscal-quarter measurement period.
units.notes: A hard 20% cap shared across three add-back categories - a classic shared-cap relationship a pipeline could miss.

units.description: Notwithstanding the EBITDA definition, EBITDA is deemed to be fixed dollar amounts for four historical quarters: Q1 2021 $24,044,000; Q2 2021 $26,146,000; Q3 2021 $23,253,000; Q4 2021 $21,919,000, and adjustments used to derive those figures may not be reused after December 31, 2021.
units.notes: Hardwired historical EBITDA for LTM builds through Q4 2022 - directly changes early ratio results.

units.description: 'Applicable EBITDA' means EBITDA of the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries for the four consecutive fiscal quarters most recently ended for which financials have been delivered under Section 5.01(a)/(b) (or, pre-first delivery, the Section 3.04(a) financials).
units.notes: Denominator for every percentage-of-EBITDA basket in Article VI (6.01(b)(iii)/(c)(iii)/(p)/(q), 6.02(p), 6.04(r), 6.05(k)) and for the Available Amount clause (i).

units.description: 'Total Indebtedness' = aggregate principal amount of all Indebtedness of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries on a consolidated basis, but EXCLUDING clauses (i) (letters of credit/letters of guaranty) and (m) (Swap Agreement obligations) of the 'Indebtedness' definition.
units.notes: The (i)/(m) carve-outs materially reduce the leverage numerator - undrawn LCs and swap MTM are excluded.

units.description: 'Total Net Leverage Ratio' = (Total Indebtedness minus Unrestricted Cash, with cash netting capped at $25,000,000) divided by EBITDA for the four most recently ended consecutive fiscal quarters. Operating leases reflected on the balance sheet are excluded from the calculation.
units.notes: Cash netting is capped at $25M and only Unrestricted Cash (control-agreement cash of Loan Parties) counts.

units.description: 'Interest Coverage Ratio' = EBITDA divided by Consolidated Interest Expense for a four-quarter period. For the 'Annualized Quarters' ending 3/31/2022, 6/30/2022, 9/30/2022 and 12/31/2022, Consolidated Interest Expense is annualized by multiplying post-Effective-Date interest expense by 4, 2, 4/3 and 1 respectively.
units.notes: The annualization convention changes the covenant result for the first four test dates.

units.description: 'Consolidated Interest Expense' (and the near-identical 'Interest Expense') means total interest expense including Capital Lease Obligations, LC/bankers' acceptance commissions and discounts, and net costs under interest-rate Swap Agreements, on a consolidated GAAP basis.
units.notes: Two nearly identical defined terms ('Consolidated Interest Expense' and 'Interest Expense') both exist; Interest Coverage uses Consolidated Interest Expense, EBITDA add-back (a)(i) uses Interest Expense.

units.description: 'Net Income' means consolidated net income (loss) of the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries under GAAP, excluding (a) pre-acquisition income of any Person before it became a Restricted Subsidiary and (b) income of non-Restricted-Subsidiary equity investees except to the extent actually received in cash dividends.

'Unrestricted Cash' means unrestricted cash and Permitted Investments held by the Loan Parties on a consolidated basis, only to the extent subject to account control agreements in favor of the Administrative Agent.
units.notes: Control-agreement condition means cash at non-Loan-Party subsidiaries never nets against leverage. Also used in the Permitted Acquisition $10,000,000 liquidity test.

units.description: 'Consolidated Total Assets' means the aggregate book value of consolidated total assets of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries per the most recent Section 5.01 financials.
units.notes: Used only in the Material Subsidiary 5%/10% tests.

units.description: 'Indebtedness' has a thirteen-clause definition (a)-(m) covering borrowed money, notes/bonds, obligations bearing interest, conditional sale obligations, earn-outs and deferred purchase price (excluding ordinary-course trade payables, unaccrued earn-outs, accrued expenses), non-recourse secured debt of others (capped at property FMV), Guarantees, Capital Lease Obligations, LC reimbursement obligations, bankers' acceptances, Off-Balance Sheet Liabilities, Disqualified Stock, and Swap Agreement obligations.
units.notes: The earn-out carve-out (only counted once reflected as a balance-sheet liability and unpaid when due) is economically significant for acquisition-heavy borrowers.

units.description: 'Capital Lease Obligations' means obligations required to be classified as capital or finance lease obligations under GAAP, measured at the capitalized amount.
units.notes: Interacts with Section 1.04's GAAP-change protections and the Total Net Leverage Ratio operating-lease exclusion.

units.description: 'Off-Balance Sheet Liability' means (a) repurchase obligations with respect to sold accounts/notes receivable and (b) synthetic lease obligations; it is a component of Indebtedness clause (k).
units.notes: Interacts with Permitted Supply Chain Financing, which is structured as a true sale to avoid this.

units.description: 'Permitted Acquisition' means the TEquipment Acquisition and any Acquisition by a Loan Party satisfying eleven conditions (a)-(k): not hostile; same/related line of business; no Default before or after on a pro forma basis; 20 days' prior notice with draft documents, due diligence package and third-party quality-of-earnings report for acquisitions >= $50,000,000; structured as asset purchase, merger with a Loan Party surviving, or purchase of substantially all voting Equity Interests; Loan Party must survive any merger; target must have positive pro forma adjusted EBITDA; pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 AND Total Net Leverage Ratio at least 0.25x inside the then-applicable 6.12(b) level AND Availability plus Unrestricted Cash of at least $10,000,000; Section 5.13 collateral/joinder actions taken; 5 Business Days' prior officer's certificate for acquisitions > $50,000,000; and a lifetime cap of $50,000,000 on aggregate consideration for acquisitions of non-Loan-Parties/non-Collateral assets.
units.notes: Clause (h)(ii) is a 0.25x inside-the-covenant cushion measured against the level INCLUDING any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment; clause (k) is a hard $50M lifetime non-guarantor/non-collateral basket.

units.description: 'Acquisition' means any transaction or related series consummated on or after the Effective Date by which a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary acquires a going business or substantially all assets of a Person, or a majority of voting or outstanding Equity Interests of a Person.
'Material Acquisition' means (a) the TEquipment Acquisition and (b) any acquisition with aggregate total consideration in excess of $75,000,000.
units.notes: Sole gating trigger for the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment (leverage covenant holiday) in Section 6.12(b).

units.description: 'Permitted Encumbrances' means ten categories (a)-(j) of non-consensual/ordinary-course Liens: tax Liens not yet due or contested per 5.04; carriers'/warehousemen's/mechanics' Liens not overdue by more than 60 days or contested; workers' compensation and social security deposits; bid/performance/surety/appeal bond deposits; judgment Liens not constituting an Event of Default under 7.01(k); easements/zoning/rights-of-way not securing monetary obligations; customary trading and brokerage account margin deposits; contractual setoff rights on depository, sweep and purchase-order arrangements; utility/municipal security deposits; and Governmental Authority Liens for non-delinquent or contested Canadian Priority Payables. Excludes any Lien securing Indebtedness except under clauses (d) and (e).
units.notes: Incorporated by reference into Section 6.02(b) as a standing Lien exception and into the 3.15 priority representation.

units.description: 'Permitted Investments' means five categories (a)-(e) of cash-equivalent investments: U.S./Canadian government obligations maturing within one year; highest-rated commercial paper maturing within 270 days; CDs, bankers' acceptances and time deposits maturing within 180 days at banks with capital and surplus of at least $500,000,000; fully collateralized 30-day repos; and AAA/Aaa money market funds with at least $5,000,000,000 in assets.
units.notes: Feeds both Section 6.04(a) (permitted investments basket) and the Unrestricted Cash definition.

units.description: 'Prepayment Event' means (a)(i) any Disposition made in reliance on Section 6.05(k), (a)(ii) any Disposition of all or substantially all assets or Equity Interests of an Unrestricted Subsidiary, (a)(iii) any casualty or condemnation event, or (b) any incurrence of Indebtedness not permitted under Section 6.01.
units.notes: Only 6.05(k) sales trigger the sweep - all other permitted Dispositions escape mandatory prepayment. Clause (b) is a non-permitted-debt sweep.

units.description: 'Net Proceeds' means cash proceeds of a Prepayment Event (including deferred payments as received, insurance proceeds and condemnation awards) less third-party fees and expenses, amounts required to repay other Indebtedness secured by the asset, and taxes paid or reserved that are directly attributable to the event.

'Restricted Payment' means any dividend or distribution on Equity Interests of a Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary, or any payment on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of such Equity Interests or of options/warrants therefor.

'Restricted Subsidiary' means any Subsidiary other than an Unrestricted Subsidiary; 'Unrestricted Subsidiary' means any Subsidiary designated as such on Schedule 3.14 on the Effective Date or designated by the Company's board under Section 5.15 and not since redesignated.
units.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: substantially every covenant in Articles V and VI binds only Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries; every ratio is computed for the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries only.

units.description: 'subsidiary' means an entity consolidated with the parent under GAAP or in which the parent holds more than 50% of equity, ordinary voting power or general partnership interests, or which is otherwise Controlled; 'Subsidiary' means any direct or indirect subsidiary of a Borrower or Loan Party, defaulting to subsidiaries of the Company.

'Material Subsidiary' means each Restricted Subsidiary (excluding non-U.S. and non-Canadian Subsidiaries) contributing more than 5% of EBITDA for the most recent four-quarter period or more than 5% of Consolidated Total Assets; plus, if non-Material Subsidiaries in the aggregate exceed 10% of EBITDA or 10% of Consolidated Total Assets, the Company (or, after 10 days, the Administrative Agent) must designate additional U.S. Subsidiaries first, then Canadian Subsidiaries, to eliminate the excess.
units.notes: Drives which subsidiaries must join as guarantors and pledge collateral under Section 5.13(a), and which can be released under 10.08(b).

units.description: 'Material Indebtedness' means Indebtedness (other than the Loans and Letters of Credit) or Swap Agreement obligations of the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries in an aggregate principal amount exceeding $20,000,000; Swap Agreement principal is measured as the net termination amount.
units.notes: Sets the cross-default (7.01(f)) and cross-acceleration (7.01(g)) threshold at $20M, and the Section 5.04 payment covenant scope.

units.description: 'Material Adverse Effect' means a material adverse effect on (a) business, assets, operations or financial condition of the Borrowers and Restricted Subsidiaries taken as a whole, (b) any Loan Party's ability to perform material Obligations, (c) the Collateral or the Administrative Agent's Liens on a material portion thereof or their priority, or (d) the rights or benefits of the Agent, Issuing Bank or Lenders under the Loan Documents.

'Change in Control' occurs on (a) acquisition by any Person or group other than a Permitted Owner of more than 30% of the Company's aggregate ordinary voting power, (b) a majority of the Company's board seats occupied by persons who were not directors on the closing date nor nominated/appointed by the incumbent board, or (c) the Company ceasing to own 100% of the outstanding voting Equity Interests of the other Borrowers free of Liens. 'Permitted Owner' means any Person that as of the Effective Date owns more than 30% of the Company's voting power.
units.notes: The Permitted Owner carve-out effectively grandfathers the existing LKCM-affiliated control block; a Change in Control is a standalone Event of Default under 7.01(m).

units.description: The credit is bifurcated: 'U.S. Loan Parties' (U.S. Borrowers plus U.S. Loan Guarantors) and 'Canadian Loan Parties' (Canadian Borrowers plus Canadian Loan Guarantors); 'Loan Parties' means both collectively. 'Loan Guarantor' means each Loan Party.
units.notes: ENTITY-APPLICABILITY: the U.S./Canadian split is enforced throughout (2.01 final paragraph, 5.13(e)(i), 6.09(b), 10.01(b), 11.07(a)) - Canadian Loan Parties never guarantee or secure U.S. Secured Obligations.

units.description: 'U.S. Secured Obligations' = Obligations of U.S. Loan Parties plus Banking Services Obligations and Swap Agreement Obligations of U.S. Loan Parties and U.S. Subsidiaries owing to Lenders/Affiliates; 'Canadian Secured Obligations' = the parallel Canadian set, and expressly excludes any U.S. Secured Obligations. Neither creates a guarantee or security interest supporting Excluded Swap Obligations.
units.notes: This one-way ring-fence is the single most distinctive structural feature of the collateral/guarantee package.

units.description: 'Obligations' captures all principal, LC Exposure, fees, expenses, indemnities and other liabilities of Loan Parties to Lenders, Agent, Issuing Bank or Indemnitees, including post-petition interest. 'Secured Parties' includes Lenders, the Agent, each Issuing Bank, Banking Services providers, Swap counterparties (to the extent their obligations are Secured Obligations), indemnitees and successors.

'Required Lenders' means Lenders holding more than 50% of Aggregate Credit Exposure plus Unfunded Commitments (pre-acceleration) or of Aggregate Credit Exposure (post-acceleration); Unfunded Commitments are deemed zero solely for accelerating under 7.02; Swingline Exposure in excess of a Lender's Applicable Percentage is excluded; and Affiliate Lenders are disregarded except as permitted by 9.04(f).
units.notes: Voting-power definition; interacts with 2.20(c) (Defaulting Lender disenfranchisement) and 9.04(f)(iv) (Affiliate Lender voting sterilization, Debt Fund Affiliate 25% cap).

units.description: 'Affiliate Lenders' means LKCM Headwater Investments III, L.P. and its Affiliates (excluding the Company/Subsidiaries and natural persons); 'Debt Fund Affiliate' is an Affiliate that is a Bona Fide Debt Fund with information walls; 'Bona Fide Debt Fund' is defined by primary lending activity and independent fiduciary duties.
units.notes: Sponsor-affiliate debt buyback architecture; the 20% Affiliate Lender Cap lives in Section 9.04(f)(i)(D).

units.description: 'Disqualified Institutions' means Persons designated by the Borrower Representative on or before the Effective Date as disqualified institutions or Competitors, plus name-identifiable Affiliates, subject to a supplement mechanic effective two Business Days after delivery and non-retroactive; a Bona Fide Debt Fund is not a Disqualified Institution unless named under clause (a)(i).
units.notes: Assignment restriction with real economic effect; Disqualified Institutions are 'Ineligible Institutions' barred from assignments under 9.04.

units.description: 'Disqualified Stock' means equity that matures, is mandatorily redeemable, is putable at the holder's option, or converts into Indebtedness or Disqualified Stock, in each case prior to 91 days after the latest Maturity Date (with change-of-control/IPO/asset-sale exceptions subordinated to Payment in Full, and a management-equity carve-out). 'Qualified Stock' is Equity Interests other than Disqualified Stock.
units.notes: Disqualified Stock counts as Indebtedness (clause (l)); only Qualified Stock proceeds build the Available Amount or fund a Specified Equity Contribution.

units.description: 'Permitted Supply Chain Financing' means one or more non-recourse supply chain financings on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent in respect of Accounts, provided the sale is a true sale with recourse limited to breaches of representations/warranties/covenants.
units.notes: Enables the 6.01(o) debt basket, the 6.02(o) Lien basket and the 6.05(j) Disposition basket - a three-way linked exception.

units.description: 'Subordinated Indebtedness' means Indebtedness the payment of which is subordinated to the Secured Obligations to the Administrative Agent's written reasonable satisfaction.
units.notes: Gates Section 1.07 (senior designation), 6.08(b)(ii) (no payments prohibited by subordination terms) and 6.11(a) (no adverse amendments).

units.description: Facility sizing: aggregate Revolving Commitments $200,000,000; aggregate Initial Term Loan Commitments $250,000,000; aggregate Delayed Draw Term Loan Commitments $50,000,000; Swingline Commitment per the Commitment Schedule ($10,000,000 for JPMorgan); Issuing Bank Sublimit $25,000,000 for JPMorgan. All three Maturity Dates are April 1, 2027; the Delayed Draw Term Loan Availability Period runs to the earlier of October 1, 2022 and termination of the DDTL Commitments.
keyDefinedTerms: Delayed Draw Term Loan Maturity Date
Delayed Draw Term Loan Availability Period

units.description: 'Dutch Auction' sets out full auction procedures for the Company or a Subsidiary to purchase Term Loans: Auction Notice specifying an Auction Amount of at least $5,000,000 in $1,000,000 increments and a Discount Range; Return Bids in $1,000,000 increments (one bid per Lender); Applicable Discount determination, Failed Auction withdrawal or completion at the lowest Reply Discount; pro rata allocation among Qualifying Bids; and mandatory sale by any Lender submitting a Qualifying Bid.
units.notes: Operative machinery for both the Section 9.04(f) Affiliate Lender assignments and the Section 9.04(g) loan buybacks.

units.description: 'Paid in Full'/'Payment in Full' requires cash payment of all Loans, LC Disbursements and accrued interest; termination/cash collateralization of all Letters of Credit at 103% of LC Exposure; payment of fees and reimbursable expenses and other Secured Obligations (excluding unasserted contingent obligations); termination of all Commitments; and termination of or satisfactory arrangements for Swap Agreement and Banking Services Obligations.
units.notes: Sets the endpoint of the Article V and VI covenant periods and the release triggers in 9.02(c) and 10.08(c).

units.description: 'Guarantee' captures any contingent obligation having the economic effect of guaranteeing another Person's Indebtedness, including purchase/pay obligations, keep-well/net-worth maintenance obligations, and account-party LC obligations, excluding ordinary-course collection endorsements; measured at the stated or maximum reasonably anticipated amount.

'Disposition'/'Dispose' covers any sale, transfer, license, lease or other disposition, expressly including Sale and Leaseback Transactions and dispositions effected pursuant to a Division. 'Division', 'Dividing Person' and 'Division Successor' capture Delaware-style LLC divisions.
units.notes: Anti-Delaware-LLC-division drafting; reinforced by Section 1.09 and the Section 6.03(b) prohibition on Divisions.

units.description: 'Returns' means any dividend, distribution, interest, fee, premium, return of capital, principal repayment, income or profit realized on an investment; 'Not Otherwise Applied' means an amount not previously or simultaneously applied to another use under the Loan Documents.
units.notes: Both are anti-double-counting mechanics inside the Available Amount build.

units.description: Definitions for the two Effective Date acquisitions: the Gexpro Acquisition (of 301 HW Opus Holdings, Inc. under the 12/29/2021 merger agreement) and the TestEquity Acquisition (of TestEquity Acquisition, LLC under the 12/29/2021 merger agreement), plus Closing Date Acquisition Documents, Closing Date Acquisition Agreement Representations, Closing Date Material Adverse Effect, Closing Date Target Indebtedness (payoff debt including the January 2022 GS Operating facility and the 2017 TestEquity/NXT Capital facility) and Closing Date Transaction Expenses.
units.notes: These support the Section 4.01(b) certain-funds conditions and the EBITDA (a)(vi) 180-day transaction-expense add-back.

units.description: Benefit-plan definitions: ERISA Event (seven enumerated triggers), Plan, Multiemployer Plan, Withdrawal Liability, ERISA Affiliate, Benefit Plan, Plan Asset Regulations, PTE; and the Canadian analogues Canadian Pension Plans, Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan and Canadian Pension Event (termination causing liability, contribution failures creating priority Liens, improper withdrawals).
units.notes: Feed the 5.02(d) notice trigger ($5M) and the 7.01(l) Event of Default ($20M), and the 6.03(g) prohibition on Canadian defined benefit plans.

units.description: Sanctions cluster: Sanctions (U.S., Canadian, UN, EU, UK measures), Sanctioned Country (as of signing: so-called DPR and LPR, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria), Sanctioned Person, Anti-Corruption Laws, Canadian Economic Sanctions and Export Control Laws, OFAC, CAML, USA PATRIOT Act.
units.notes: Gate the 3.20 representation, the 5.07/5.08(b) covenants and the 2.06(a) LC issuance limits.

units.description: 'Canadian Priority Payables' means amounts secured by Liens that rank or may rank prior to or pari passu with the Collateral Document Liens, including wages, vacation and severance pay, source deductions, sales/excise/income tax, workers compensation, government royalties and Canadian Pension Plan contributions.
units.notes: Statutory-priority leakage specific to the Canadian collateral pool; also a Permitted Encumbrance under clause (j).

units.description: Collateral architecture definitions: Collateral, Collateral Documents, Security Agreements (the amended and restated U.S. Pledge and Security Agreement and the amended and restated Canadian Pledge and Security Agreement), Excluded Property (defined in the applicable Security Agreement), Loan Documents, and Loan Guaranty (Article X).
units.notes: 'Excluded Property' is defined only by cross-reference to the Security Agreements, which are not part of this document - a genuine cross-document dependency.

units.description: Interest-rate benchmark definitions (grouped): ABR, Alternate Base Rate (with a 1.00% floor on the resulting ABR), Adjusted Term SOFR Rate and Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR (each SOFR plus 0.10%), Term SOFR Rate/Reference Rate, Daily Simple SOFR, SOFR, CDOR Rate/Screen Rate, Canadian Prime Rate, Prime Rate, NYFRB Rate, Federal Funds Effective Rate, Overnight Bank Funding Rate, Floor (zero), Interest Period (1/3/6 months for Term Benchmark; 30/90 days for CDOR), Interest Payment Date, Type, Class, Benchmark, Benchmark Replacement, Benchmark Replacement Adjustment/Conforming Changes/Date, Benchmark Transition Event, Benchmark Unavailability Period, Available Tenor, Relevant Rate, Reference Time.
units.notes: Note the unusual 1.00% ABR floor built into the 'Alternate Base Rate' definition. Otherwise standard 2022 SOFR-transition machinery.

units.description: Tax definitions (grouped): Taxes, Excluded Taxes (including Canadian Part XIII non-arm's-length/specified shareholder withholding), Indemnified Taxes, Other Taxes, Other Connection Taxes, Connection Income Taxes, FATCA, ITA, Recipient, Foreign Lender, U.S. Person, U.S. Tax Compliance Certificate.

Remaining ordinary/administrative definitions grouped and not individually itemized: Account, Account Debtor, Administrative Agent, Administrative Questionnaire, Affiliate, Agreed Currency, Alternative Currency, Ancillary Document, Applicable Percentage, Applicable Time, Approved Electronic Platform, Approved Fund, Arranger, Assignment and Assumption, Availability, Availability Period, Bail-In definitions, Banking Services, Bankruptcy Code/Event, Beneficial Ownership Certification/Regulation, BHC Act Affiliate, Borrowing, Borrowing Request, Burdensome Restrictions, Business Day, CAM definitions, Charges, Code, Commitment Schedule, Commodity Exchange Act, Communications, Company, Compliance Certificate, Control, Credit Exposure, Credit Party, Default, Defaulting Lender, Disclosed Matters, Dollar/Dollar Equivalent, Document, ECP, EEA definitions, Effective Date, Electronic Signature/System, Environmental Laws/Liability, Equipment, Equity Interests, Equivalent Amount, Exchange Rate, Existing Credit Agreement, Existing Letters of Credit, Financial Officer, Fixtures, Foreign Subsidiary, Funding Account, GAAP, Governmental Authority, Hazardous Materials, Insolvency Laws, IRS, Issuing Bank, Joinder Agreement, JPMorgan, LC Collateral Account/Disbursement/Exposure, Lenders, Letters of Credit, Liabilities, Lien, Loans, Margin Stock, Maturity Date, Moody's, Parent, Participant, Payment, PBGC, Person, PPSA, Proceeding, Projections, Qualified ECP Guarantor, Register, Regulations D/T/U/X, Related Parties, Release, Report, Requirement of Law, Resolution Authority, Responsible Officer, Revaluation Date, Revolving Exposure/Lender/Loan, RFR, S&P, SEC, SOFR administration terms, Statements, Swap Agreement/Obligation, Swingline definitions, UCC, UK definitions, Unfunded Commitments, U.S. definitions.
units.notes: Grouped by design: these are definitional-only with no independent operative effect beyond the sections that use them.

units.description: Loans and Borrowings may be classified and referred to by Class, by Type, or by Class and Type. Purely nomenclature.

Interpretive conventions: singular/plural, 'including' means without limitation, references to agreements as amended, 'will' equals 'shall'; UCC-defined terms carry PPSA equivalents; and a lengthy Quebec civil-law equivalence table (hypothec, movable/immovable property, solidary liability, etc.) for Quebec Collateral.
units.notes: The Quebec/PPSA translation provisions are interpretive but are what make the Canadian collateral package function.

units.description: Accounting terms follow GAAP as in effect from time to time, but either the Borrower Representative or the Required Lenders may freeze a provision at pre-change GAAP by requesting an amendment to neutralize a GAAP change (frozen pending withdrawal or amendment). All computations must ignore fair-value elections under ASC 825-10-25 and must value convertible debt (ASC 470-20) at full stated principal.
units.notes: A GAAP-freeze notice can change every ratio and basket result; note GAAP means U.S. GAAP for U.S. Loan Parties and Canadian GAAP for Canadian Loan Parties.

units.description: Benchmark discontinuation notification and full Administrative Agent disclaimer of responsibility for rate administration or the economics of any replacement rate.

Pro forma calculation rules: for any permitted Acquisition or out-of-ordinary-course Disposition in the trailing four quarters, or any transaction requiring pro forma calculation, the Total Net Leverage Ratio and Interest Coverage Ratio are computed giving pro forma effect (Regulation S-X Article 11 basis, Financial Officer certified) as if the transaction occurred on the first day of the period, by reference to the most recently delivered financials; pro forma compliance is tested against the Section 6.12 level WITHOUT giving effect to any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment (except when testing Permitted Acquisition conditions); proceeds of Indebtedness incurred in the transaction may not be counted as Unrestricted Cash; and floating-rate debt is annualized at the rate in effect on the determination date.
units.notes: The exclusion of the Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment from pro forma tests (other than Permitted Acquisitions) is easy to miss and directly changes basket availability during a covenant-holiday period.

units.description: If any Loan Party has Subordinated Indebtedness outstanding, it must cause the Secured Obligations to constitute 'senior indebtedness' and 'designated senior indebtedness' thereunder so the Lenders can exercise payment blockage and other senior-creditor remedies; the Secured Obligations are hereby so designated.
Financial ratios are calculated by carrying the quotient to one more decimal place than the ratio is expressed and rounding to the nearest number (rounding up if there is no nearest number).
units.notes: Directly affects borderline covenant compliance calls.

units.description: For all Loan Document purposes, a Delaware-style division that moves an asset or liability to a different Person is deemed a transfer, and any new Person created is deemed organized and acquired on its first day of existence by its equity holders.
units.notes: Closes the LLC-division loophole for the transfer/investment/asset-sale covenants.

units.description: The Administrative Agent or Issuing Bank determines Dollar Equivalents of Alternative Currency Borrowings and Letters of Credit on each Revaluation Date, which govern until the next Revaluation Date; expressly excluded from financial-statement preparation and financial covenant calculation. Dollar-denominated minimums apply as Dollar Equivalents to Alternative Currency transactions.
units.notes: The carve-out for financial covenant calculations means FX revaluation drives borrowing-base/exposure tests but not leverage/coverage.

units.description: This Agreement amends, supersedes and restates the October 11, 2019 Existing Credit Agreement in its entirety without novation: existing liens, guarantees and obligations continue and are re-evidenced hereunder; Existing Credit Agreement 'Commitments' continue as Revolving Commitments; the Administrative Agent may effect reallocations/assignments among Lenders without assignment fees; accrued interest and fees plus break costs under the Existing Credit Agreement are payable on the Effective Date; and each Loan Party ratifies and reaffirms its prior guarantees and Lien grants.
units.notes: Determines which agreement is operative and preserves perfection continuity - directly relevant to 'which version is operative today'.

units.description: (a) Revolving Lenders severally commit to make Revolving Loans in Dollars, Canadian dollars or another Alternative Currency during the Availability Period, subject to each Lender's Revolving Commitment and the aggregate Revolving Commitments (revolving, so borrow/prepay/reborrow permitted); (b) Initial Term Lenders make a single $250,000,000 Initial Term Loan in Dollars to the Company on the Effective Date, non-reborrowable; (c) Delayed Draw Term Lenders make Delayed Draw Term Loans in Dollars during the Delayed Draw Term Loan Availability Period, non-reborrowable.

Closing flush language: notwithstanding anything to the contrary, no Canadian Loan Party is obligated to repay, support or guarantee any U.S. Secured Obligations or any other U.S. Loan Party obligation, and payments made by a Canadian Loan Party are applied only to Canadian Secured Obligations.
units.notes: ENTITY-APPLICABILITY: the operative statement of the one-way Canadian ring-fence, reinforced in 5.13(e)(i), 10.01(b) and 11.07(a).

units.description: Borrowing mechanics: several (not joint) Lender obligations; currency/Type matching by Class; minimum Borrowing sizes ($500,000 with $100,000 multiples for revolving/term-benchmark; $5,000,000 with $1,000,000 multiples for Delayed Draw Term Loans; $100,000 with $50,000 multiples for Swingline); a cap of six Term Benchmark/RFR Borrowings and six CDOR Borrowings outstanding; and no Interest Period extending past the applicable Maturity Date.

Borrowing Request mechanics and notice deadlines (three Business Days for Term Benchmark/CDOR; noon same day for ABR/Canadian Prime; 9:00 a.m. for LC reimbursement financings), required contents, deemed elections, and an express prohibition on requesting RFR Loans (Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR applies only via Sections 2.14(a) and (f)).

Currency-of-payment indemnity: obligations denominated in a relevant currency are discharged only to the extent of the amount of that currency purchasable with the payment made; the Borrower or Guarantor indemnifies any shortfall as a separate obligation, and excess is remitted back.

Swingline Loans: discretionary (the Swingline Lender 'may agree, but shall have no obligation'), Dollar-only, to U.S. Borrowers only, subject to the Swingline Commitment and revolving sublimits; the Swingline Lender may require Revolving Lenders to fund participations on an absolute and unconditional basis notwithstanding any Default; replacement and resignation mechanics on 30 days' notice.
units.notes: Swingline availability is discretionary, not committed - relevant to actual liquidity capacity.

units.description: Letters of Credit: aggregate LC Exposure sublimit of $25,000,000 (plus per-Issuing-Bank Issuing Bank Sublimits); issuance conditioned on no Revolving Commitment/exposure breach; Sanctions-related refusal rights; one-year maximum tenor and expiry no later than five Business Days before the Revolving Credit Maturity Date (longer only with cash collateral); mandatory 103% cash collateralization on the Revolving Credit Maturity Date; Revolving Lender participations; reimbursement within one Business Day of notice with an option to finance via ABR/Canadian Prime/Swingline Borrowing; absolute obligations; LC Collateral Account cash collateral at 103% on an Event of Default (automatic for bankruptcy Events of Default under 7.01(h)/(i)); Existing Letters of Credit deemed issued hereunder.
units.notes: The $25,000,000 LC sublimit sits inside the $200,000,000 Revolving Commitments - a nested capacity relationship.

units.description: Lender funding mechanics to the Administrative Agent's account by 2:00 p.m. Chicago time and the customary agent-may-assume-funding provision with several repayment obligations of the Lender and the Borrowers.

Conversion/continuation mechanics; no Interest Period non-compliant elections, no currency changes, no Swingline conversions; deemed one-month (Term Benchmark) or 30-day (CDOR) continuations absent an election; and during a continuing Event of Default (at Required Lender request) no Term Benchmark or CDOR conversions/continuations, with existing Borrowings converting to ABR or Canadian Prime.

(a)-(d) Commitment termination and voluntary reduction: Initial Term Loan Commitments terminate on funding or 5:00 p.m. on the Effective Date; Revolving Commitments terminate on the Revolving Credit Maturity Date; DDTL Commitments terminate dollar-for-dollar on funding and at the end of the Delayed Draw Term Loan Availability Period. Voluntary reductions in $1,000,000 multiples with three Business Days' notice, permanent and ratable, with conditional-notice revocation permitted if tied to a refinancing.

(e)-(i) Incremental facility: the Borrowers may increase Revolving Commitments or add Incremental Term Loan tranches, from existing Lenders or new lenders (excluding Ineligible Institutions), subject to a $5,000,000 minimum per request and an aggregate incremental cap of $200,000,000; Agent (and, for revolver increases, Swingline Lender and Issuing Bank) approval of new lenders; conditions precedent of reaffirmed representations, no Default, and pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 (including any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment) assuming the full amount is drawn; Incremental Term Loans rank pari passu, may not mature before the latest existing Maturity Date, must have no shorter weighted average life, and must be treated no more favorably than existing loans (though they may be priced differently and may carry additional covenants applicable only after the latest Maturity Date). No Lender is committed to provide any increase. Affiliate Lenders providing Incremental Term Loans must first comply with Section 9.04(f).
units.notes: $200,000,000 total incremental capacity is a hard dollar cap (no ratio-based freebie); note there is NO MFN/most-favored-nation pricing protection - pricing may differ freely.

units.description: Repayment and amortization: Revolving Loans due on the Revolving Credit Maturity Date and Swingline Loans on the earlier of that date and the fifth Business Day after funding (with automatic repayment from Revolving Loan proceeds); Initial Term Loans amortize $3,125,000 per quarter on the last day of March, June, September and December beginning June 30, 2022 (1.25% of the original $250,000,000 per quarter), balance due at the Initial Term Loan Maturity Date; Delayed Draw Term Loans amortize at 1.25% of the original funded principal per quarter, commencing after full draw or expiry of the DDTL availability period but not before June 30, 2022; amortization amounts are adjusted by Sections 2.11(e) and 2.18(b). Evidence-of-debt and promissory note provisions.
keyDefinedTerms: Delayed Draw Term Loan Maturity Date

units.description: The Borrowers may prepay any Borrowing in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty, subject to notice under 2.11(d) and break funding under Section 2.16.
units.notes: No call protection or prepayment premium on any tranche.

units.description: If the Dollar Equivalent of Aggregate Revolving Exposure exceeds the aggregate Revolving Commitments, the Borrowers must prepay or cash collateralize the excess; if caused solely by currency fluctuation, no prepayment is required until exposure exceeds 102% of the Revolving Commitments, and in no event may the excess persist for more than two consecutive Business Days.
units.notes: The 102% FX cushion is a real, easily-missed operational allowance.

units.description: Mandatory prepayment of Term Loans in an amount equal to 100% of Net Proceeds of any Prepayment Event, within three Business Days for asset sale/casualty events and one Business Day for non-permitted debt incurrences, subject to (i) an annual $10,000,000 de minimis threshold for asset-sale/casualty proceeds (the 'Asset Sale Prepayment Trigger', with only amounts above the threshold swept) and (ii) a reinvestment right: proceeds reinvested in assets useful to the business within 12 months, or 18 months total if a binding commitment is made within 12 months, escape the sweep; failure to reinvest requires prepayment within five Business Days.
units.notes: CRITICAL: no excess cash flow sweep exists in this agreement; the asset-sale sweep only reaches Section 6.05(k) sales and only above $10M per fiscal year.

units.description: Prepayment notice deadlines by Type (three Business Days Term Benchmark/CDOR, five for RFR, one for ABR/Canadian Prime, same day for Swingline); irrevocability with a conditional-refinancing exception; partial prepayment minimums; ratable application within a Class; accompanied by accrued interest and break funding.

Mandatory prepayments under 2.11(c) are applied ratably across all Classes of Term Loans and, within each Class, first to accrued and unpaid interest, then ratably to the next four scheduled amortization payments, and then ratably to all remaining scheduled repayments including the balloon at maturity.
units.notes: The 'first four scheduled repayments then ratably' waterfall is a specific, non-standard application order.

units.description: Foreign Prepayment Event carve-out: Net Proceeds of a Foreign Subsidiary that are legally prohibited or delayed from repatriation, or whose repatriation the Company determines in good faith would have adverse tax consequences (including Section 956 deemed dividends or withholding tax), need not be applied until repatriation is permitted or tax-neutral; non-application is expressly not a Default and the retained amounts may be used for working capital or general corporate purposes.

Any Term Lender may decline all (but not less than all) of its share of a mandatory prepayment by delivering a Rejection Notice by 12:00 p.m. one Business Day before the payment date; failure to do so is deemed acceptance. Declined Amounts are retained by the Borrowers and their Restricted Subsidiaries as 'Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts'.
units.notes: Borrower Retained Prepayment Amounts flow directly into the Available Amount builder (clause (vii)) - a linkage between the prepayment mechanics and Article VI basket capacity.

units.description: Fees: commitment fee at the Applicable Rate on undrawn Revolving Commitments (LC Exposure counts as drawn, Swingline Exposure does not); ticking fee at the Applicable Rate on unused Delayed Draw Term Loan Commitments; LC participation fees at the Term Benchmark/CDOR Applicable Rate and separately negotiated fronting fees to each Issuing Bank; agency fees per separate fee letter; all fees on a 360-day basis and non-refundable.
units.notes: Note the unusual Swingline exclusion from the commitment-fee 'drawn' calculation.

units.description: Interest: ABR/Canadian Prime Loans at the base rate plus Applicable Rate; Term Benchmark and CDOR Loans at the applicable rate for the Interest Period plus Applicable Rate; RFR Loans at Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR plus Applicable Rate. Default interest: during a continuing Event of Default, the Administrative Agent or Required Lenders may (optional, by notice, revocable) impose +2.00% on all Loans, +2.00% on Section 2.12(b) fees, and +2.00% on any other overdue amount. Day-count conventions (360 days, or 365/366 for Prime-based ABR, CDOR and Canadian Prime), Canadian Interest Act disclosure and criminal-rate (Section 347 Criminal Code (Canada)) adjustment mechanics.
units.notes: Default interest is elective and requires notice, not automatic - a meaningful distinction on default consequences.

units.description: Standard 2022-vintage benchmark unavailability, Benchmark Transition Event / Benchmark Replacement, Benchmark Replacement Conforming Changes, tenor removal/reinstatement, and Benchmark Unavailability Period fallback provisions, including negative-consent Required Lender objection for non-Dollar replacements.

Customary increased-costs and capital-adequacy yield protection for Changes in Law, with a certificate conclusive absent manifest error, ten-day payment, and a 180-day look-back limitation (extended for retroactive Changes in Law).
Customary break funding indemnity for off-cycle payment, conversion, failure to borrow, assignment under 2.19/9.02(d), or Alternative Currency payment failure, for Term Benchmark, CDOR and RFR Loans.

Customary tax gross-up for Indemnified Taxes, Other Taxes payment, indemnification by Loan Parties and by Lenders, full Status of Lenders documentation regime (W-9, W-8BEN/BEN-E, W-8ECI, W-8IMY, U.S. Tax Compliance Certificates, FATCA), refund-sharing, and survival.

Payment mechanics and, in subsection (b), the application waterfall for non-specified payments and for all payments after an Event of Default at the Agent's election or Required Lenders' direction: first Agent/Swingline/Issuing Bank fees, indemnities and expenses; second Lender fees, indemnities and expenses; third accrued interest ratably; fourth principal, unreimbursed LC Disbursements, and Swap Agreement and Banking Services Obligations (up to the amounts most recently notified under Section 2.22) ratably; fifth 103% of LC Exposure as cash collateral; sixth all other Secured Obligations. Amounts from a Loan Party are never applied to that party's Excluded Swap Obligations. Subsection (d) is a customary pro rata sharing-of-setoffs provision.
units.notes: Swap/Banking Services obligations share the fourth tier with principal only up to the amount most recently notified under 2.22 - otherwise they drop to the sixth tier.

units.description: Mitigation obligations (designating a different lending office) and a yank-a-bank right allowing the Borrowers to require a Lender claiming increased costs or tax gross-up, or any Defaulting Lender, to assign its interests at par plus accrued amounts, subject to Agent consent and a resulting reduction in the claimed amounts.

Defaulting Lender regime: commitment fees cease to accrue on the Defaulting Lender's Unfunded Commitments; an eight-tier waterfall for payments otherwise due to it; voting disenfranchisement (excluded from Required Lender calculations except for consents requiring each affected Lender); reallocation of Swingline and LC Exposure to non-Defaulting Lenders up to their Revolving Commitments, with prepayment/cash collateralization of any unreallocated portion; fee adjustments; and suspension of Swingline and LC issuance obligations (extended to Lender Parent Bankruptcy Events and good-faith belief of other funding defaults).
Clawback/revival provision: if a payment is later surrendered as a preference or otherwise, the Obligations are revived and continued; survives termination.

Each Lender or Affiliate providing Banking Services or Swap Agreements to a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary must notify the Administrative Agent of the aggregate amount of such obligations, updating after significant changes or on request; the most recent information determines the waterfall tier under Section 2.18(b). JPMorgan and its Affiliates are exempt from this notice requirement while JPMorgan is Administrative Agent.
units.notes: The notice requirement is what converts hedging/cash-management exposure into meaningfully secured claims at tier four of the waterfall.

units.description: Each Loan Party (not merely the Borrowers) represents and warrants to the Lenders as to the matters in Sections 3.01 through 3.22.
units.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: representations are given by every Loan Party but most are qualified to Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries, excluding Unrestricted Subsidiaries.

units.description: Each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary is duly organized, validly existing, in good standing, has requisite power, and is qualified where required except where failure could not reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect.

The Transactions are within each Loan Party's organizational powers, duly authorized, and each Loan Document is a legal, valid and binding obligation subject to customary bankruptcy and equitable exceptions.

The Transactions require no Governmental Authority consents other than those obtained and perfection filings; will not violate any Requirement of Law; will not violate or create a default or payment right under any binding indenture or agreement (each subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier); and will not create any Lien on material assets other than Liens created under the Loan Documents.

(a) The audited consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2021 (BDO USA LLP) present fairly in all material respects. (b) No event, change or condition has occurred that has had or could reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect since December 31, 2021.
units.notes: The 3.04(a) financials are the fallback reference set for every 'most recent financial statements' calculation before the first Section 5.01 delivery.

units.description: (a) Schedule 3.05 lists owned and leased real property; leases are valid and in full force absent Material Adverse Effect; Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries have good title or valid leaseholds free of Liens other than those permitted by Section 6.02. (b) Ownership or license of all necessary intellectual property, with registered IP listed on Schedule 3.05 and no material infringement.

No pending or threatened proceedings (other than Disclosed Matters on Schedule 3.06) with a reasonable possibility of adverse determination that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect, or involving any Loan Document or the Transactions; no material Environmental Liability claims or non-compliance outside the Disclosed Matters; and no change in the status of Disclosed Matters increasing the likelihood of a Material Adverse Effect.

Each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary is in compliance with all Requirements of Law and binding agreements, subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier, and no Default has occurred and is continuing.
No Loan Party or Subsidiary is an 'investment company' under the Investment Company Act of 1940.

All required Tax returns filed and Taxes paid, except contested Taxes with adequate reserves or where failure could not be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect; no material tax liens filed or claims asserted.

(a) No ERISA Event has occurred or is reasonably expected that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect, and Plan accumulated benefit obligations do not exceed Plan asset fair value. (b) As of the Effective Date none of the Canadian Pension Plans (listed on Schedule 3.10(b)) is a Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, with five sub-representations on registration, administration, disputes, benefit improvements and contributions.
units.notes: The 'no Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan' representation pairs with the Section 6.03(g) prohibition on incurring one.

units.description: (a) Full disclosure of agreements, restrictions and matters that could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect; information furnished contains no material misstatement or omission, with a good-faith/reasonable-assumptions standard for projections. (b) Beneficial Ownership Certification information is true and correct as of the Effective Date.

Solvency representation tested for the Loan Parties taken as a whole immediately after the Transactions and after each Loan and Letter of Credit: asset fair value exceeds debts; present fair saleable value exceeds probable liabilities; ability to pay debts as they mature; no unreasonably small capital; and each Canadian Loan Party is not an 'Insolvent Person' under the BIA. Plus a no-intent-to-incur-unpayable-debts representation.
units.notes: Tested on a 'taken as a whole' basis for Loan Parties, not entity by entity - relevant to fraudulent-transfer analysis alongside Sections 10.10 and 10.11.

units.description: Schedule 3.13 describes all insurance maintained as of the Effective Date; premiums due are paid; insurance is believed adequate and customary.

As of the Effective Date, Schedule 3.14 lists each Subsidiary and its relationship to the Borrowers, each class of authorized Equity Interests and record ownership, entity type, and whether each Subsidiary is a Loan Party, Material Subsidiary, Restricted Subsidiary or Unrestricted Subsidiary.
units.notes: Schedule 3.14 is the Effective Date designation of Unrestricted Subsidiaries referenced in the 'Unrestricted Subsidiary' definition; the schedule itself is not reproduced in this document.

units.description: The Loan Documents create legal, valid, perfected and continuing first-priority Liens on the Collateral in favor of the Administrative Agent for the Secured Parties upon the making of specified filings (UCC, PPSA, USPTO, U.S. Copyright Office, CIPO) and delivery of possessory collateral, subject only to Permitted Encumbrances with statutory priority and Liens perfected only by possession not held by the Agent.
As of the Effective Date, no pending or threatened strikes, lockouts or slowdowns; wage/hour compliance subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier; wage and benefit payments made or accrued.

No Loan Party is engaged principally in purchasing or carrying Margin Stock; no proceeds will be used to buy or carry Margin Stock; not more than 25% of asset value will be Margin Stock; no violation of Regulation U or X.
Loan proceeds have been and will be used as set forth in Section 5.08.
No Loan Party is subject to any Burdensome Restrictions except those permitted under Section 6.10.
units.notes: Ties the negative-pledge/dividend-blocker representation directly to the Section 6.10 exception list.

units.description: Policies and procedures are maintained to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and Sanctions; Loan Parties, Subsidiaries, officers and directors are in material compliance and none is a Sanctioned Person; no Borrowing, Letter of Credit or use of proceeds will violate Anti-Corruption Laws or Sanctions.
No Loan Party is an Affected Financial Institution (EEA/UK bail-in regime).

No Loan Party or Subsidiary holds 'plan assets' under the Plan Asset Regulations, and the transactions will not give rise to a non-exempt prohibited transaction under ERISA Section 406 or Code Section 4975.

The Lenders' obligation to lend and the Issuing Bank's obligation to issue Letters of Credit do not become effective until every Section 4.01 condition is satisfied or waived under Section 9.02; any reference to Loan Parties in Section 4.01 includes Persons that become Loan Parties immediately following the Closing Date Acquisitions.

Receipt of executed counterparts of this Agreement and the other Loan Documents, requested promissory notes, and U.S. and Canadian counsel legal opinions, all satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.

Closing Date Acquisition conditions: (i) each Closing Date Acquisition consummated in all material respects per its acquisition agreement substantially concurrently, without amendments materially adverse to Lenders; (ii) no Closing Date Material Adverse Effect since December 29, 2021; (iii) Closing Date Acquisition Agreement Representations true and correct; (iv) no injunction or legal action prohibiting closing; and (v) delivery of specified financial information (audited FY2021 statements for the Company and each Closing Date Target, unaudited quarterlies, projections through 2026 with assumptions, quality of earnings reports, and a Regulation S-X pro forma balance sheet and income statement).
units.notes: This is a limited-conditionality ('certain funds') construct: the acquisition-agreement representation standard is limited to those representations whose breach would permit the Company to decline to close.

units.description: Secretary's certificates with resolutions, incumbency and attached organizational documents for each Loan Party, plus good standing certificates.
Financial Officer's closing certificate as to no Default, truth of representations, and satisfaction of the conditions in Sections 4.01(b)(i), (ii) and (iii).

Payment of all fees and invoiced expenses (invoices presented at least two Business Days before closing) and of all accrued interest and fees owing under the Existing Credit Agreement, funded with proceeds of Effective Date Loans.

Recent lien and intellectual property search results in each Loan Party's jurisdiction of organization and asset locations showing no Liens other than those permitted by Section 6.02 or discharged via payoff letters.

Satisfactory payoff letters for all Closing Date Target Indebtedness confirming termination and release of all Liens and Guarantees, with existing letters of credit cash collateralized or backstopped.
Notice designating the Funding Account for transfer of Borrowing proceeds, plus a customary funding indemnification letter for any Term Benchmark or CDOR Rate Loan.
Solvency certificate signed by a Financial Officer of the Borrower Representative, in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent.

Delivery of certificates representing pledged Equity Interests with undated stock powers, and endorsed promissory notes/possessory collateral; the certificate requirement is NOT a condition to funding if commercially reasonable efforts were used, with a five-day post-closing delivery obligation.

All UCC, PPSA and federal intellectual property filings required to perfect first-priority Liens must be in proper form for filing; together with 4.01(j), most perfection steps other than UCC/PPSA filings, certificated equity delivery and short-form IP filings are converted into 30-day (or five-day for certificated equity) post-closing obligations rather than funding conditions.
units.notes: The flush proviso following 4.01(k) is a genuine limited-conditionality collateral carve-out, not boilerplate.

units.description: Evidence of insurance coverage satisfactory to the Administrative Agent and complying with Section 5.10 and the Security Agreements, subject to Section 5.14 post-closing requirements.
Completed letter of credit application if a Letter of Credit is required on the Effective Date, plus execution of the Issuing Bank's master commercial LC agreement.
The Administrative Agent and its counsel shall have completed all legal due diligence with results satisfactory to the Administrative Agent in its SOLE discretion.
units.notes: A sole-discretion diligence condition is unusually broad for a limited-conditionality acquisition financing.

units.description: Delivery, at least five days before the Effective Date, of KYC/anti-money-laundering documentation requested at least ten days in advance, IRS Forms W-8/W-9 for each Loan Party, and any requested Beneficial Ownership Certification (deemed satisfied on a requesting Lender's execution).
Such other documents as the Administrative Agent, Issuing Bank, any Lender or their counsel may reasonably request.

Closing flush language: the Administrative Agent's notice of the Effective Date is conclusive and binding; and if the conditions are not satisfied or waived by 2:00 p.m. Chicago time on June 30, 2022, the Commitments terminate automatically at that time.
units.notes: A hard commitment-termination outside date, not merely a milestone.

units.description: Each Borrowing and each LC issuance/amendment/renewal/extension is conditioned on (a) representations being true and correct in all material respects (in all respects for materiality-qualified representations, and only as of the specified date for dated representations) and (b) no Default having occurred and continuing; each credit event is deemed a representation to that effect. Notwithstanding failure of these conditions, the Administrative Agent may (but need not), unless the Required Lenders direct otherwise, continue to make Loans and issue Letters of Credit for the ratable account and risk of the Lenders if it believes doing so is in the Lenders' best interests.
units.notes: The discretionary protective-advance override in the final paragraph is a genuinely operative Agent right, not boilerplate.

units.description: Until all Secured Obligations are Paid in Full, each Loan Party executing the Agreement covenants jointly and severally with all other Loan Parties to comply with Article V.
units.notes: ENTITY SCOPE: covenants bind Loan Parties and (where stated) Restricted Subsidiaries - Unrestricted Subsidiaries are outside the covenant perimeter.

units.description: Financial statements and other information: (a) audited annual consolidated financials within 90 days of fiscal year end (or the SEC Form 10-K deadline including automatic extensions), commencing FY2022, without going-concern or scope qualification; (b) quarterly financials within 45 days of the end of each of the first three fiscal quarters (or the Form 10-Q deadline), commencing Q1 2022; (c) a Compliance Certificate with each delivery, certifying fair presentation, whether a Default exists, detailed Section 6.12 calculations, and a Restricted/Unrestricted Subsidiary list where relevant; (d) annual Projections within 45 days after fiscal year end; (e) public SEC filings and shareholder materials; (f) SEC investigation correspondence; (g) accountant management letters on request; (h) other information and KYC/Beneficial Ownership information on request; (i) ERISA Section 101(k)/(l) Multiemployer Plan documents on request; and (j) consolidating Company/Restricted Subsidiary statements whenever Unrestricted Subsidiaries exist. Electronic delivery via EDGAR or a website is deemed delivery.
units.notes: Clauses (c)(iii)/(c)(iv) and (j) are the mechanism by which the Restricted/Unrestricted perimeter and covenant compliance are actually reported. Late delivery deems Category 1 pricing under the Applicable Rate definition and triggers a 5-day cure Event of Default under 7.01(e)(i).

units.description: Prompt written notice of: (a) any Default; (b) governmental investigations or litigation seeking damages over $5,000,000, injunctive relief over material assets, claims against a Plan, material criminal misconduct, material Environmental Law violations, tax or governmental charge liability over $5,000,000, or any material product recall; (c) any material change in accounting or financial reporting practices other than as required by GAAP; (d) any ERISA Event or Canadian Pension Event that could reasonably be expected to result in aggregate liability exceeding $5,000,000; (e) any development resulting in or reasonably expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect; and (f) any change to the Beneficial Ownership Certification. Each notice must be accompanied by a Financial Officer's statement of details and remedial action.
units.notes: Breach of 5.02(a) alone is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with no cure period; breaches of the other 5.02 clauses get a 5-day cure under 7.01(e)(i).

units.description: Each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary will preserve its legal existence and material rights, licenses, permits, franchises, governmental authorizations and intellectual property, and maintain qualification to do business, and will conduct business in substantially the same fields as at closing or reasonably related fields; the covenant does not prohibit mergers, liquidations or dissolutions permitted by Section 6.03.
units.notes: Breach of 5.03 with respect to a Loan Party's EXISTENCE is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with no cure period; other 5.03 breaches get 30 days under 7.01(e)(ii).

units.description: Each Loan Party and Restricted Subsidiary will pay or discharge all Material Indebtedness and other material liabilities including Taxes before delinquency where non-payment could reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect, except where contested in good faith with adequate GAAP reserves and non-payment pending contest could not result in a Material Adverse Effect.
units.notes: The contest exception is cross-referenced by Permitted Encumbrances clauses (a) and (b).

units.description: Keep and maintain all property material to the conduct of business in good working order and condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted.

Keep proper books and records and permit Agent/Lender representatives (including consultants and appraisers) to visit, inspect, examine books and discuss affairs with officers and accountants on reasonable notice; absent a continuing Event of Default, no more than one visit or inspection per year; during a continuing Event of Default the Agent and Lenders may also conduct field examinations at Loan Party premises. Reports may be prepared and distributed to Lenders.
units.notes: The one-inspection-per-year limit and the Event-of-Default field-exam right are real, negotiated economics; breach carries only the 5-day cure of 7.01(e)(i).

units.description: Comply with all Requirements of Law (including Environmental Laws) subject to a Material Adverse Effect qualifier, and maintain and enforce policies and procedures designed to ensure compliance with Anti-Corruption Laws and applicable Sanctions.

(a) Initial Term Loan proceeds finance the Effective Date Transactions with the remainder for working capital and general corporate purposes; Revolving Loans, Swingline Loans and Letters of Credit fund working capital and general corporate purposes (expressly including the Effective Date Transactions, Permitted Acquisitions and Restricted Payments); Delayed Draw Term Loan proceeds may be used SOLELY to finance the TEquipment Acquisition and other Permitted Acquisitions and related fees and expenses; no proceeds may violate Regulations T, U or X. (b) No Borrowing or Letter of Credit may be used in violation of Anti-Corruption Laws or Sanctions or to fund activities with a Sanctioned Person or in a Sanctioned Country.
units.notes: The DDTL use-of-proceeds restriction is a hard purpose limitation. Breach of 5.08 is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with no cure period.

units.description: Information furnished by or on behalf of a Loan Party in connection with the Loan Documents will contain no material misstatement or omission, with furnishing deemed a representation to that effect; Projections must be prepared in good faith on reasonable assumptions, with a standard forward-looking-information disclaimer.

Maintain with financially sound and reputable carriers insurance customary for similar businesses (with no greater risk retention) and all insurance required by the Collateral Documents; furnish detail on request but at least annually.
Reserved - no operative content.

Prompt written notice of casualty or insured damage to, or condemnation proceedings affecting, any material portion of the Collateral, and assurance that Net Proceeds of any such event are collected and applied per this Agreement and the Collateral Documents.
units.notes: Links to the Prepayment Event definition clause (a)(iii) casualty/condemnation sweep.

units.description: (a) Within 30 days after any Person becomes a U.S. or Canadian Subsidiary that is also a Material Subsidiary, or after any such Subsidiary qualifies or is designated as a Material Subsidiary, the Company must deliver a Joinder Agreement and Security Agreement joinder with resolutions and (if requested) opinions, whereupon the Person becomes a Loan Guarantor and grants Liens on its Collateral (excluding U.S. real property); guarantee/joinder is excused where it would produce a material adverse tax consequence or where cost/burden outweighs value. (b) All owned property other than Excluded Property must be subject to first-priority perfected Liens, and 100% of the Equity Interests of directly owned Restricted Subsidiaries must be pledged, subject to the same tax/cost-benefit exception. (c) Further assurances. (d) Post-closing acquired material assets must be collateralized on request. (e) Three overriding limitations: (i) U.S. Secured Obligations are never secured by Canadian Loan Party Collateral; (ii) no Collateral Documents or perfection actions are required outside the U.S. and Canada; and (iii) the Administrative Agent may unilaterally waive perfection where cost is disproportionate to benefit.
units.notes: CRITICAL entity-scope provision: determines who becomes a guarantor and what is pledged. The material-adverse-tax-consequence and cost/benefit escapes, plus the no-non-US/Canada-perfection rule, materially limit the collateral package. Breach carries only a 5-day cure under 7.01(e)(i).

units.description: The Loan Parties must take the actions set forth on Schedule 5.14 by the dates specified there (or such later dates as the Administrative Agent agrees in its sole discretion).
units.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: the entire operative content of this covenant lives on Schedule 5.14, which is NOT reproduced in this filed exhibit, so neither the required actions nor their deadlines can be determined from this document. The stakes are high - breach is an immediate Event of Default under Section 7.01(d) with no cure period - so materiality could be anywhere from INFORMATIONAL to CRITICAL depending on schedule content that is not available here.

units.description: The Company may designate any Restricted Subsidiary as Unrestricted, or any Unrestricted Subsidiary as Restricted, if: (a) before and after giving pro forma effect, no Default exists and the Company is in pro forma compliance with Section 6.12; (b) no Loan Party may be designated Unrestricted; (c) no Subsidiary may be designated Unrestricted if it would be a 'Restricted Subsidiary' for any other secured Indebtedness; (d) no Unrestricted Subsidiary may own Equity Interests in a Restricted Subsidiary or hold a Lien on Loan Party/Restricted Subsidiary property; and (e) no Unrestricted Subsidiary may own intellectual property material to the business (non-exclusive ordinary-course licenses permitted). Designation as Unrestricted constitutes an investment under Section 6.04 measured at designation; redesignation as Restricted constitutes incurrence of that Subsidiary's investments, Indebtedness and Liens and a return on investment.
units.notes: CRITICAL: this is the trap-door for moving assets outside the covenant perimeter; the IP restriction in clause (e) plus the 6.05 flush IP prohibition are the anti-drop-down protections.

units.description: Until all Secured Obligations are Paid in Full, each Loan Party executing the Agreement covenants jointly and severally with all other Loan Parties to comply with Article VI.
units.notes: Any breach of Article VI is an immediate Event of Default under 7.01(d) with NO cure or grace period.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or suffer to exist any Indebtedness, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (q).
The Secured Obligations and the Guaranteed Obligations under the Loan Documents themselves.

Intercompany Indebtedness of any Borrower owed to a Restricted Subsidiary and of any Restricted Subsidiary owed to a Borrower or another Restricted Subsidiary, provided (i) debt of non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries owed to a Borrower or Loan Party is subject to Section 6.04, (ii) debt of a Loan Party owed to a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary must be subordinated to the Secured Obligations on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Agent, and (iii) the aggregate principal amount of debt of non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries owed to U.S. Loan Parties, TOGETHER WITH Guarantees under 6.01(c)(iii) and investments under 6.04(b), may not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: SHARED CAP: 6.01(b)(iii), 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b) share a single 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap on U.S.-Loan-Party exposure to non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries. Note 6.04(b)'s own text says '15% of EBITDA' rather than Applicable EBITDA - an internal drafting inconsistency.

units.description: Guarantees by any Borrower of Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness and by any Restricted Subsidiary of Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary Indebtedness, provided (i) the underlying debt is permitted by Section 6.01, (ii) Guarantees by a Loan Party of non-Loan-Party debt are subject to Section 6.04, and (iii) Guarantees by U.S. Loan Parties of non-U.S.-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary debt, together with 6.01(b)(iii) debt and 6.04(b) investments, may not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: Second leg of the shared 15% of Applicable EBITDA cap.

units.description: Indebtedness owed to providers of workers' compensation, health, disability, employee benefits or property/casualty/liability insurance under reimbursement or indemnification obligations, incurred in the ordinary course.
Indebtedness of any Loan Party in respect of performance bonds, bid bonds, appeal bonds, surety bonds and similar obligations provided in the ordinary course of business.
units.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN (entity applicability): the basket is uncapped but by its terms extends only to 'any Loan Party', whereas the Section 6.01 chapeau restricts both Loan Parties AND Restricted Subsidiaries and most sibling clauses (e.g. (l), (m), (p)) expressly cover 'the Company or any Restricted Subsidiary'. It is unclear from the text whether a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary may incur ordinary-course performance/bid/appeal/surety bond obligations at all.

units.description: Indebtedness existing on the Effective Date and listed on Schedule 6.01, plus any Refinance Indebtedness in respect thereof.
units.notes: Schedule 6.01 is not reproduced in this document, so the grandfathered amount cannot be determined from this text.

units.description: Refinance Indebtedness extending, renewing, refinancing or replacing Section 6.01(f) Original Indebtedness, subject to six conditions: no increase in principal (other than unused commitments, accrued interest, fees, defeasance costs, premiums, discounts and expenses); no extension of Liens to additional property (other than accessions and after-acquired property); no new obligors; no shortening of weighted average maturity; terms not less favorable to the obligor; and subordination terms at least as favorable if the Original Indebtedness was subordinated.
units.notes: This is the general refinancing conduit and is also incorporated into 6.01(p) for purchase-money debt.

units.description: Acquired/assumed Indebtedness of any Person designated as a Restricted Subsidiary after the Effective Date, provided it existed before and was not created in contemplation of that Person becoming a Restricted Subsidiary, and capped at $20,000,000 outstanding at any time.
units.notes: Hard $20,000,000 cap; note the clause is drafted around designation as a Restricted Subsidiary rather than acquisitions generally (6.01(m) covers Permitted Acquisition debt).

units.description: Customer deposits and advance/progress payments received in the ordinary course from customers, to the extent constituting Indebtedness.

Indebtedness in respect of Banking Services, netting services, overdraft protection, employee credit card programs, automatic clearinghouse and similar deposit-account arrangements incurred in the ordinary course, and obligations arising from honoring checks drawn against insufficient funds.

Letters of support, guarantees or similar obligations issued for the benefit of the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary as required by law or in connection with statutory filings or audit opinions in non-U.S. jurisdictions, in the ordinary course.
Indebtedness consisting of insurance premium financing or take-or-pay obligations in supply arrangements, incurred in the ordinary course or consistent with past practice.

Indebtedness of the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary incurred, assumed or issued in connection with a Permitted Acquisition, and Indebtedness of Persons acquired or merged into the Company or a Restricted Subsidiary pursuant to a Permitted Acquisition.
units.notes: UNCAPPED acquisition-debt basket - capacity is governed indirectly by the Permitted Acquisition conditions (pro forma leverage 0.25x inside the covenant, liquidity test) rather than by any dollar or ratio limit here.

units.description: Indebtedness from customary indemnification, purchase price adjustment and similar obligations (including earn-outs) incurred in connection with a Permitted Acquisition, other permitted Section 6.04 acquisition, or a Section 6.05 Disposition.
Obligations under one or more Permitted Supply Chain Financings, to the extent constituting Indebtedness.
units.notes: Paired with the 6.02(o) Lien basket and 6.05(j) Disposition basket.

units.description: Purchase money and capital lease Indebtedness incurred to finance the acquisition, construction or improvement of fixed or capital assets (including assumed debt secured by a Lien on such assets), plus permitted refinancings under clause (g), provided the debt is incurred within 180 days of the acquisition or completion and the aggregate, together with related Refinance Indebtedness, does not exceed 15% of Applicable EBITDA at any time outstanding.
units.notes: Grower basket expressed solely as a percentage of Applicable EBITDA with no dollar floor; secured by the corresponding 6.02(j) Lien basket.

units.description: General Indebtedness basket: other Indebtedness in an aggregate outstanding principal amount not exceeding the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: Greater-of grower basket. Note it is NOT expressly conditioned on absence of a Default.
