units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create, incur, assume or permit to exist any Lien on any property or asset now owned or hereafter acquired, or assign or sell any income, revenues (including Accounts) or rights, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (p).
Liens created pursuant to any Loan Document.
Permitted Encumbrances (the ten-category definitional list in Section 1.01).

Liens existing on the Effective Date and set forth on Schedule 6.02, provided they do not extend to other property and secure only the obligations they secured on the Effective Date plus non-increasing extensions, renewals and replacements.
units.notes: Schedule 6.02 is not reproduced in this document.

units.description: Liens existing on property prior to its acquisition, or on property of a Person before it becomes a Restricted Subsidiary (excluding designation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary as Restricted), provided the Lien was not created in contemplation, does not extend to other property, and secures only pre-existing obligations plus non-increasing refinancings.
units.notes: The express exclusion of Unrestricted-to-Restricted redesignations closes a leakage path.

units.description: Collecting bank Liens under UCC Section 4-210 (or PPSA equivalent) on items being collected, and bankers' Liens and customary contractual setoff rights on deposit and securities accounts, in each case not given in connection with Indebtedness.
Liens arising out of Sale and Leaseback Transactions permitted by Section 6.06.
Liens granted by a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary in favor of a Borrower or another Loan Party securing Indebtedness owed by that Restricted Subsidiary.

Liens in favor of customs and revenue authorities arising by law to secure customs duties on imported goods, and Liens on specific inventory or goods securing bankers' acceptances or documentary letters of credit facilitating their purchase, shipment or storage.
Liens arising from conditional sale, title retention, consignment or similar arrangements for the sale of goods in the ordinary course, not extending to other property.

Purchase money Liens on fixed or capital assets acquired, constructed or improved, provided they secure Indebtedness permitted by Section 6.01(p), are incurred within 180 days of the acquisition or completion, do not exceed the cost of the asset, and do not extend to other property.
units.notes: Capacity is derivative of the 6.01(p) 15% of Applicable EBITDA basket - a linked debt/Lien pair.

units.description: Liens under workers' compensation, unemployment insurance, employee benefit and similar legislation; good-faith bid, tender, contract and lease deposits; public/statutory obligation Liens; cash or U.S. government bond deposits securing surety, stay, customs, performance or appeal bonds; rent deposits and contractual/warranty refund deposits; plus Liens securing letters of credit, bankers acceptances or bank guaranties supporting the foregoing.

Ordinary-course leases, franchises, subleases, licenses, sublicenses (non-exclusive as to intellectual property), covenants not to sue, releases and consents that do not materially interfere with the business and do not secure Indebtedness.
Liens arising from UCC or similar financing statement filings regarding ordinary-course operating leases or consignments.
Purported Liens (other than securing Indebtedness for borrowed money) evidenced by precautionary UCC or equivalent filings incurred in the ordinary course.
Liens on Accounts sold (or, upon judicial recharacterization, granted as collateral) pursuant to any Permitted Supply Chain Financing.
General Lien basket: other Liens securing obligations in an aggregate principal amount at any time outstanding not exceeding the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA.
units.notes: Mirrors the 6.01(q) general debt basket in size but is a SEPARATE basket - the two are not expressly linked, so obligations could in principle use 6.01(q) capacity and 6.02(p) capacity independently.

units.description: No merger, consolidation, amalgamation, Disposition of all or substantially all assets or of all or substantially all Restricted Subsidiary stock, liquidation or dissolution, except (if no Event of Default exists or would result): (i) a Canadian Subsidiary may merge into a Borrower with a Borrower surviving (a U.S. Borrower must survive any transaction involving a U.S. Borrower); (ii) a U.S. Subsidiary may merge into a U.S. Borrower with the U.S. Borrower surviving; (iii) a Canadian Loan Party (non-Borrower) may merge into another Loan Party with a Loan Party surviving (a U.S. Loan Party must survive if a U.S. Loan Party is involved); (iv) a non-Borrower U.S. Loan Party may merge into another U.S. Loan Party; and (v) a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary may liquidate or dissolve if the Borrowers determine in good faith it is in their best interests and not materially disadvantageous to Lenders. Any merger involving a non-wholly-owned Restricted Subsidiary must also be permitted by Section 6.04.
units.notes: The survivorship rules are drafted to preserve the U.S./Canadian ring-fence - a Canadian entity may never end up as the surviving entity where a U.S. Loan Party is involved.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may consummate a Division as the Dividing Person without the Administrative Agent's prior written consent; if an LLC Loan Party nonetheless divides, each Division Successor that is a Material Subsidiary must comply with Section 5.13 and become a Loan Party.
No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may engage in any business other than businesses of the type conducted on the Effective Date and reasonably related businesses and reasonable extensions.
No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may change its fiscal year or any fiscal quarter from the basis in effect on the Effective Date.
units.notes: Prevents manipulation of four-quarter covenant measurement periods.

units.description: No Loan Party may change the accounting basis on which its financial statements are prepared, except as required by GAAP or directed by the SEC.
units.notes: Works together with the Section 1.04 GAAP-freeze mechanic.

units.description: No Loan Party may change the tax filing elections it has made under the Code.

No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may contribute to, assume or incur liability under any Canadian Defined Benefit Pension Plan, or acquire an interest in any Person that sponsors, maintains or contributed to one within the preceding five years, without the Administrative Agent's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld).
units.notes: An acquisition-blocking covenant: it can prohibit an otherwise-Permitted Acquisition of a target with Canadian DB plan history.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, form any subsidiary after the Effective Date, or acquire or hold Equity Interests, evidences of indebtedness or securities of, make or permit loans or advances to, Guarantee obligations of, or make or hold any investment in, any other Person, or acquire assets constituting a business unit, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (r).
units.notes: Note the covenant also restricts the mere FORMATION of new subsidiaries after the Effective Date.

units.description: Permitted Investments (the cash-equivalents list in Section 1.01).

Investments by Loan Parties in Equity Interests of their Restricted Subsidiaries that are Loan Parties, provided such Equity Interests are pledged under the applicable Security Agreement; and further provided that the aggregate outstanding amount of investments by U.S. Loan Parties in Restricted Subsidiaries that are not U.S. Loan Parties made after the Effective Date, together with 6.01(b)(iii) Indebtedness and 6.01(c)(iii) Guarantees, may not at any time exceed 15% of EBITDA.
units.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: this clause is unquestionably important (it is the third leg of the shared 15% cap and would otherwise be CRITICAL), but its own scope is ambiguous on the face of the text - it says '15% of EBITDA' while the parallel provisos in 6.01(b)(iii) and 6.01(c)(iii) describing the SAME shared cap say '15% of Applicable EBITDA'. 'EBITDA' and 'Applicable EBITDA' are separately defined terms with different measurement conventions, so the size of the shared cap cannot be determined with confidence from this text.

units.description: Intercompany loans and advances by a Loan Party to another Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, and by a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary to a Loan Party or another Restricted Subsidiary, provided (i) loans made by a Loan Party are evidenced by a promissory note pledged under the applicable Security Agreement and (ii) loans by U.S. Loan Parties to non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiaries are subject to the 6.01(b)(iii) cap determined without regard to write-downs or write-offs.
units.notes: The 'without regard to write-downs or write-offs' language prevents rebuilding capacity by impairing intercompany loans.

units.description: Guarantees permitted under Section 6.01.
Notes payable or stock/securities issued by account debtors to a Loan Party under negotiated settlements of Accounts in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.
Investments in the form of Swap Agreements permitted by Section 6.07.

Investments constituting deposits described in clauses (c) and (d) of the 'Permitted Encumbrances' definition (workers' compensation/social security deposits and bid/trade contract/lease/surety bond deposits).

Permitted Acquisitions (as fully conditioned in the Section 1.01 definition, including the pro forma leverage cushion of 0.25x, the $10,000,000 Availability-plus-Unrestricted-Cash liquidity test, and the $50,000,000 lifetime cap on non-Loan-Party/non-Collateral consideration).
units.notes: The primary acquisition basket - unlimited in size except through the Permitted Acquisition conditions.

units.description: Investments existing at the time a Person becomes a Restricted Subsidiary (excluding via designation of an Unrestricted Subsidiary as Restricted) or consolidates or merges with a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, so long as not made in contemplation of that event.
The Closing Date Acquisitions (Gexpro and TestEquity).

Investments existing on the Effective Date and described on Schedule 6.04, plus modifications, replacements, renewals, refinancings, reinvestments and extensions that do not increase the amount except per the investment's own terms plus accrued interest, PIK amounts, premium, fees and expenses as in existence on the Effective Date.
units.notes: Schedule 6.04 is not reproduced in this document.

units.description: (i) Arms-length loans and advances (and Guarantees) to employees in the ordinary course for travel, entertainment, relocation and similar purposes, capped at $5,000,000 outstanding at any one time; and (ii) non-cash loans to officers, directors, governors, managers and employees used simultaneously to purchase Qualified Stock of the Company.
units.notes: $5,000,000 hard cap on cash employee loans; the non-cash equity-purchase loans in (ii) are uncapped.

units.description: Investments consisting of ordinary-course purchases and acquisitions of inventory, supplies, materials, equipment or similar assets or services.
Non-exclusive licensing of intellectual property in the ordinary course, or that does not materially interfere with the business and does not secure Indebtedness.
units.notes: Must be read with the Section 6.05 flush prohibition on transferring material IP to Unrestricted Subsidiaries and Section 5.15(e).

units.description: Deposits required by any Governmental Authority or public utility, including with respect to Taxes and similar charges, to the extent the underlying obligations would not constitute an Event of Default.

Investments in prepaid expenses, negotiable instruments held for collection, and lease, utility, workers compensation, performance and similar deposits entered into in the ordinary course of business.

Available Amount investments: other investments not exceeding the Available Amount immediately prior to the investment, so long as at the time and after giving pro forma effect (i) no Event of Default exists or would result and (ii) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than 0.50x below the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: consumes the same Available Amount as Section 6.08(a)(iv) Restricted Payments, and usage under either reduces the Available Amount via clause (viii) of its definition. Requires a 0.50x leverage cushion.

units.description: General investment basket: other investments, loans and advances in an aggregate outstanding amount not exceeding the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA, measured at the time made, provided no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing or would result.
units.notes: Unlike 6.01(q) and 6.02(p), this general basket IS conditioned on no Event of Default.

units.description: Flush valuation rules for Sections 5.15 and 6.04: designating a Subsidiary as Unrestricted is an 'investment' equal to the Company's proportionate share of the fair market value of that Subsidiary's net assets at designation; upon redesignation as Restricted, a permanent deemed investment remains equal to the original investment less the proportionate net asset fair market value at redesignation (if positive); and property transferred to or from an Unrestricted Subsidiary is valued at fair market value at transfer.
units.notes: This is the anti-J.Crew style valuation mechanic and is easy to overlook because it sits in unlettered flush text at the end of Section 6.04.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, Dispose of any asset (including Equity Interests it owns), nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to issue additional Equity Interests other than to a Loan Party or another Restricted Subsidiary in compliance with Section 6.04, except as permitted by clauses (a) through (k).

Dispositions of (i) inventory, goods or other assets in the ordinary course; (ii) obsolete, negligible, uneconomical, worn out or surplus property; (iii) assets no longer used or useful in the business; and (iv) other property (including leasehold interests) no longer economically practical in the business.
units.notes: Uncapped and not subject to the mandatory prepayment sweep (only 6.05(k) sales are Prepayment Events).

units.description: Dispositions of assets to any Loan Party or any Restricted Subsidiary, provided that transfers (i) involving a non-Loan-Party Restricted Subsidiary or (ii) from a U.S. Loan Party to a Canadian Loan Party or vice versa must comply with Section 6.09 (affiliate transactions).
units.notes: Cross-border U.S./Canadian transfers between Loan Parties are policed through the affiliate-transaction covenant - a direct consequence of the ring-fence.

units.description: Dispositions of Accounts (excluding factoring arrangements) in connection with their compromise, settlement or collection.

Dispositions of cash, Permitted Investments and investments permitted by Sections 6.04(g) and (j); Dispositions constituting Liens permitted by Section 6.02; and Dispositions constituting Restricted Payments permitted by Section 6.08.
Sale and Leaseback Transactions permitted by Section 6.06.
Dispositions resulting from casualty, eminent domain taking, condemnation or similar proceedings affecting property of a Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary.
units.notes: Note the Net Proceeds of such events are still Prepayment Events under clause (a)(iii) of that definition.

units.description: Foreclosures, condemnation, expropriation or similar actions, Dispositions required by a Governmental Authority, and casualty or insured damage to assets.

Disposition or discount of inventory, accounts receivable or notes receivable in the ordinary course, and conversion of accounts receivable to notes receivable in the ordinary course consistent with past practice.

Ordinary-course leases, assignments, subleases, licenses, sublicenses, covenants not to sue, releases and consents (and terminations thereof) that do not materially interfere with the business taken as a whole - expressly NOT applicable to intellectual property.
units.notes: The express IP carve-out from this clause is part of the anti-IP-leakage architecture.

units.description: Dispositions resulting from sales of Accounts under Permitted Supply Chain Financings.

General asset sale basket: Dispositions of assets not permitted by any other clause (excluding Equity Interests in a Borrower, and excluding Equity Interests in any other Restricted Subsidiary unless all Equity Interests in that Restricted Subsidiary are sold), provided the aggregate fair market value of assets Disposed of in reliance on this clause does not exceed, during any fiscal year, the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA; and, other than as set forth on Schedule 6.05, all such Dispositions must be for fair value and at least 75% cash consideration.
units.notes: CRITICAL LINKAGE: this is the ONLY Disposition basket that triggers the Section 2.11(c) mandatory prepayment sweep (via clause (a)(i) of 'Prepayment Event'), and it is an annual (per fiscal year) basket rather than a cumulative one.

units.description: Flush prohibition: notwithstanding any other clause, no Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may consummate any transaction - whether by Restricted Payment, investment, Lien, sale, conveyance, transfer or other Disposition, in a single transaction or a series - resulting in the Disposition of intellectual property material to the business to any Unrestricted Subsidiary; non-exclusive ordinary-course licenses to Unrestricted Subsidiaries are permitted so long as the Company and Restricted Subsidiaries retain beneficial ownership and the same rights of use.
units.notes: Explicit anti-J.Crew blocker; overrides every other Section 6.05 exception and mirrors Section 5.15(e).

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may enter into any Sale and Leaseback Transaction, except a sale of fixed or capital assets for cash consideration not less than the asset's fair value that is consummated within 180 days after the Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary acquires or completes construction of the asset.
units.notes: Effectively limited to purchase-money-style sale-leasebacks within 180 days of acquisition; no separate dollar basket.

units.description: No Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary may enter into any Swap Agreement except (a) Swap Agreements hedging or mitigating risks to which a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary has actual exposure (other than exposure in respect of its own Equity Interests) and (b) Swap Agreements capping, collaring or exchanging interest rates with respect to an interest-bearing liability or investment.
units.notes: Anti-speculation covenant; only Swap Agreements with Lenders or Lender Affiliates become Swap Agreement Obligations sharing in the Collateral.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, declare or make (or agree or incur any obligation to make) any Restricted Payment, except as permitted by clauses (i) through (v).

Each Borrower may declare and pay dividends on its common stock payable solely in additional common stock, and on preferred stock payable solely in additional preferred stock (to the extent issuable hereunder) or in common stock.
units.notes: Stock-only dividends; no cash leakage.

units.description: Restricted Subsidiaries may declare and pay dividends ratably with respect to their Equity Interests.
units.notes: Ratable requirement protects the Loan Party group's proportionate share where minority holders exist.

units.description: Loan Parties may make Restricted Payments pursuant to and in accordance with stock option plans or other management or employee benefit plans of the Loan Parties and Restricted Subsidiaries.
units.notes: UNCAPPED management-equity basket with no dollar limit and no Default condition stated - unusually permissive.

units.description: Available Amount Restricted Payments: other Restricted Payments not exceeding the Available Amount immediately prior to the payment, so long as at the time and after giving pro forma effect (x) no Event of Default exists or would result and (y) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than 0.50x below the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: SHARED RESOURCE: draws on the same Available Amount as Section 6.04(q) investments; usage reduces the Available Amount via clause (viii) of its definition.

units.description: General dividend basket: the Company may make distributions and pay dividends to equityholders not otherwise permitted, in an aggregate amount not exceeding $10,000,000 during any fiscal year, provided (x) no Default exists immediately before or after and (y) after giving pro forma effect (including any debt incurred) the Company is in compliance with Section 6.12 WITHOUT giving effect to any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment; and any such Restricted Payment is EXCLUDED from the $10,000,000 annual limit if, after giving pro forma effect, the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than 0.50x below the maximum permitted under Section 6.12.
units.notes: CRITICAL: the final proviso converts the $10,000,000 annual cap into an UNLIMITED leverage-based dividend capacity whenever leverage is 0.50x inside the covenant - a de facto unlimited-RP-at-a-ratio construct. Also note the covenant test here expressly disregards any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment holiday.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, make or agree to make any payment or distribution of or in respect of principal or interest on any Indebtedness, or on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of any Indebtedness, except as permitted by clauses (i) through (iv).
units.notes: This is a broad restricted-debt-payment covenant reaching ALL Indebtedness, not merely subordinated or junior debt.

units.description: Payment of Indebtedness created under the Loan Documents.

Payment of regularly scheduled interest and principal as and when due on Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01, other than payments on Subordinated Indebtedness prohibited by its subordination provisions.
units.notes: Only REGULARLY SCHEDULED payments are permitted - voluntary prepayments, redemptions and open-market repurchases of other Indebtedness are prohibited unless within clauses (iii) or (iv).

units.description: Refinancings of Indebtedness to the extent permitted by Section 6.01.
Payment of secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of a voluntary sale or transfer of the property securing it, to the extent the sale or transfer is permitted by Section 6.05.
units.notes: Mirrors the corresponding carve-out from the 7.01(g) cross-acceleration Event of Default.

units.description: No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, sell, lease or transfer property or assets to, purchase or acquire property or assets from, or otherwise engage in transactions with, any of its Affiliates, except per clauses (a) through (g).
Transactions that are both in the ordinary course of business and at prices and on terms not less favorable than could be obtained on an arm's-length basis from unrelated third parties.
units.notes: Note the conjunctive test - a transaction must be BOTH ordinary course AND arm's-length; there is no fairness-opinion or board-approval alternative and no dollar de minimis.

units.description: Transactions (i) between or among the U.S. Loan Parties not involving any other Affiliate, and (ii) between or among the Canadian Loan Parties not involving any other Affiliate.
units.notes: CRITICAL: the intra-group exception is split along the U.S./Canadian ring-fence, so a transaction between a U.S. Loan Party and a Canadian Loan Party is NOT covered by this clause and must satisfy the arm's-length test of 6.09(a) - reinforced by 6.05(b)(ii).

units.description: Any investment permitted by Sections 6.04(b), 6.04(c) or 6.04(d).
Any Indebtedness permitted under Section 6.01(b) or 6.01(c).
Any Restricted Payment permitted by Section 6.08.

Payment of reasonable fees to non-employee directors of any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary, and ordinary-course compensation, employee benefit arrangements and indemnities for directors, officers and employees.
units.notes: No dollar cap on director fees or compensation arrangements.

units.description: Issuances of securities and other payments, awards or grants in cash or securities pursuant to, or the funding of, employment agreements, stock options and stock ownership plans approved by a Loan Party's board of directors.

No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, enter into, incur or permit to exist any agreement prohibiting, restricting or conditioning (a) the ability of a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary to create, incur or permit Liens on its property, or (b) the ability of any Restricted Subsidiary to pay dividends or distributions on Equity Interests, make or repay loans or advances to any Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary, or Guarantee Indebtedness of any Borrower or Restricted Subsidiary.
units.notes: Definitional hook: restrictions of the type in clauses (a) and (b) are 'Burdensome Restrictions' for purposes of the Section 3.19 representation.

units.description: The covenant does not apply to restrictions and conditions imposed by applicable law or by any Loan Document.

The covenant does not apply to restrictions existing on the Effective Date identified on Schedule 6.10, but does apply to any extension or renewal of, or amendment expanding the scope of, any such restriction.
units.notes: Schedule 6.10 is not reproduced in this document.

units.description: The covenant does not apply to customary restrictions in agreements relating to a pending sale of assets or a Restricted Subsidiary, provided the restrictions apply only to the assets or Restricted Subsidiary being sold and the sale is permitted hereunder.

Clause (a) (the anti-negative-pledge limb) does not apply to restrictions in agreements governing secured Indebtedness permitted hereunder if the restrictions apply only to the property securing that Indebtedness.
Clause (a) does not apply to customary anti-assignment provisions in leases and other contracts.

No Loan Party will, nor permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, amend, modify or waive its rights under (a) any agreement relating to Subordinated Indebtedness, (b) any Closing Date Acquisition Document, or (c) its organizational or governing documents, in each case to the extent the amendment, modification or waiver would be materially adverse to the Lenders.

MINIMUM INTEREST COVERAGE RATIO: the Company will not permit the Interest Coverage Ratio, for any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters ending on the last day of any fiscal quarter (commencing with the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2022), to be less than 3.00 to 1.00. Tested quarterly; the Interest Coverage Ratio definition annualizes Consolidated Interest Expense for the four 2022 'Annualized Quarters'.
units.notes: A maintenance covenant applicable to the Company (and therefore to all Lenders, not just Revolving Lenders); subject to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure.

units.description: MAXIMUM TOTAL NET LEVERAGE RATIO: the Company will not permit the Total Net Leverage Ratio on the last day of any fiscal quarter ending on or after June 30, 2022 to exceed (i) 4.00 to 1.00 for quarters ending on or after June 30, 2022 but prior to March 31, 2024; (ii) 3.75 to 1.00 for quarters ending on or after March 31, 2024 but prior to March 31, 2026; and (iii) 3.50 to 1.00 for quarters ending on or after March 31, 2026. Tested quarterly.
units.notes: Two hard step-downs. This level (including any Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment) is the reference point for the 0.25x Permitted Acquisition cushion and the 0.50x cushions in 6.04(q), 6.08(a)(iv) and 6.08(a)(v).

units.description: TOTAL NET LEVERAGE RATIO ADJUSTMENT: upon written request of the Borrower Representative in connection with any Material Acquisition, the maximum permitted Total Net Leverage Ratio for each of the four fiscal quarters ending immediately after the acquisition is increased by 0.50 to 1.00. The Adjustment may be used only TWICE during the term of the Agreement and only if no Event of Default has then occurred and is continuing; on notice the Agreement is automatically amended without further action.
units.notes: CRITICAL: an acquisition-triggered covenant holiday capped at two uses. It is expressly DISREGARDED for Section 1.06 pro forma tests (other than Permitted Acquisition conditions) and for the Section 6.08(a)(v) dividend test, but IS given effect for the Section 2.09(f) incremental facility condition and the Permitted Acquisition clause (h) tests - an inconsistency of scope well worth flagging.

units.description: Any of the events in Section 7.01(a) through (q) constitutes an 'Event of Default'.
Failure to pay any principal of any Loan or any LC Disbursement reimbursement obligation when due, whether at stated maturity, on a prepayment date or otherwise. NO grace period.
Failure to pay interest on any Loan, or any fee or other amount payable under any Loan Document, when due, continuing unremedied for three (3) Business Days.
units.notes: Three-Business-Day grace for non-principal payments only.

units.description: Any representation or warranty made or deemed made by or on behalf of any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary in or in connection with any Loan Document, amendment or waiver, or in any report, certificate or financial statement furnished thereunder, proves to have been incorrect in any material respect when made or deemed made. NO cure period.

Failure by any Loan Party to observe or perform any covenant contained in Section 5.02(a) (Default notice), Section 5.03 (only as to a Loan Party's existence), Section 5.08 (use of proceeds), Section 5.14 (post-closing requirements), or ANY provision of ARTICLE VI. NO grace or cure period.
units.notes: CRITICAL: every negative covenant breach - including every basket overage in Article VI and any financial covenant breach under 6.12 - is an immediate Event of Default with no cure period, subject only to the Section 7.03 Equity Cure for Section 6.12.

units.description: Failure to observe or perform any other covenant in this Agreement or any other Loan Document (other than those in 7.01(a), (b) or (d)), continuing unremedied for (i) five (5) days after the earlier of a Loan Party's knowledge or notice from the Administrative Agent, if the breach relates to Section 5.01, Section 5.02 (other than 5.02(a)), Section 5.06 or Section 5.13; or (ii) thirty (30) days after the earlier of knowledge or notice, for any other Section of this Agreement or any other Loan Document.
units.notes: The five-day tier covers financial reporting, notices, inspection rights and additional-collateral obligations - unusually short for reporting covenants.

units.description: CROSS-DEFAULT (payment): any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary fails to make any payment of principal or interest (regardless of amount) in respect of any Material Indebtedness when and as due. No grace period beyond any grace in the underlying instrument.
units.notes: Threshold is $20,000,000 via the Material Indebtedness definition; extends to Swap Agreement obligations measured at net termination value.

units.description: CROSS-ACCELERATION: any event or condition occurs that results in Material Indebtedness becoming due prior to scheduled maturity, or that enables or permits (after giving effect to grace or cure periods) the holders or their agent to cause it to become due or require prepayment, repurchase, redemption or defeasance prior to maturity; excluding secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of a voluntary sale or transfer of the securing property permitted by Section 6.05.
units.notes: This is a broad 'enables or permits' cross-acceleration - it does not require actual acceleration, so any $20M+ covenant breach elsewhere can trip this facility.

units.description: INVOLUNTARY INSOLVENCY: commencement of an involuntary case, proceeding or petition under any Insolvency Law against a Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary seeking bankruptcy/liquidation/winding-up, debt composition or reorganization relief, or appointment of a receiver, trustee, interim receiver, liquidator, administrator, custodian or similar official, that continues undismissed for sixty (60) days or results in an approving order.
units.notes: Triggers automatic acceleration and automatic LC cash collateralization under Section 7.02 and is the CAM Exchange Date trigger under Article XII.

units.description: VOLUNTARY INSOLVENCY: any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary voluntarily commences a proceeding under any Insolvency Law, consents to or fails to contest an involuntary proceeding, applies for or consents to a receiver or similar official, admits the material allegations of a petition, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or takes action to effect any of the foregoing.
units.notes: Automatic acceleration event; also a CAM Exchange Date trigger.

units.description: Any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary becomes unable, admits in writing its inability, or publicly declares an intention not to, or fails generally to, pay its debts as they become due, or any Canadian Loan Party becomes an 'insolvent person' under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada).

JUDGMENT DEFAULT: one or more money judgments aggregating in excess of $20,000,000 (excluding amounts covered by insurance where coverage is not denied) rendered against any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary and remaining undischarged and unstayed for sixty (60) consecutive days, or any judgment creditor takes legal action to attach or levy on assets; or failure within sixty (60) days to discharge non-monetary judgments that could reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.
units.notes: $20,000,000 threshold with a 60-day stay period; also feeds Permitted Encumbrances clause (e).

units.description: An ERISA Event or Canadian Pension Event has occurred that, in the opinion of the Required Lenders, together with all other such events, could reasonably be expected to result in liability of the Borrowers and Restricted Subsidiaries exceeding $20,000,000.
units.notes: Note the subjective 'in the opinion of the Required Lenders' standard.

units.description: A Change in Control shall occur (30% voting power acquisition by a non-Permitted Owner, board turnover, or the Company ceasing to own 100% of the other Borrowers' voting Equity Interests).

GUARANTY DEFAULT: the Loan Guaranty ceases to be in full force and effect (other than per its terms), any action is taken to discontinue it or assert its invalidity or unenforceability, any Loan Guarantor fails to comply with its terms, or any Loan Guarantor denies further liability or gives notice to that effect.

COLLATERAL DEFAULT: except as permitted by any Collateral Document, (i) any Collateral Document fails to create a valid security interest in purported Collateral, or (ii) any Lien securing a Secured Obligation ceases to be a perfected first-priority Lien (other than Permitted Liens).
units.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: this would otherwise be CRITICAL, but the carve-out is expressed as '(other than Permitted Liens)' and 'Permitted Liens' is NOT a defined term in Section 1.01 (the defined term is 'Permitted Encumbrances'). Reading it as the narrow 'Permitted Encumbrances' list would make any priming Lien permitted by Sections 6.02(c)-(p) an immediate Event of Default; reading it as 'Liens permitted by Section 6.02' would not. The scope of this Event of Default cannot be resolved from the text.

units.description: Any Collateral Document fails to remain in full force and effect (other than per its terms) or any action is taken to discontinue it or assert its invalidity or unenforceability.

Any material provision of any Loan Document ceases to be valid, binding and enforceable, or any Loan Party challenges enforceability or asserts (in writing or by conduct) that any provision is not valid, binding and enforceable.

Remedies: upon any Event of Default other than a 7.01(h)/(i) bankruptcy event with respect to a Borrower, the Administrative Agent may (and at Required Lender request shall), by notice, (i) terminate the Commitments including the Swingline Commitment, (ii) accelerate the Loans in whole or ratably in part with accrued interest, fees and break funding, (iii) require 103% LC cash collateral under Section 2.06(j), and (iv) exercise all rights and remedies under the Loan Documents and applicable law. Upon a 7.01(h)/(i) event with respect to a Borrower, Commitments terminate AUTOMATICALLY and the Loans, LC cash collateral obligation, interest, fees and Secured Obligations become due AUTOMATICALLY without notice. Default interest may also be imposed.
units.notes: Automatic acceleration applies only to bankruptcy events with respect to a BORROWER, not with respect to any Restricted Subsidiary - even though 7.01(h)/(i) are triggered by Restricted Subsidiary insolvency.

units.description: Secured-party remedies: the Administrative Agent may exercise all UCC/PPSA secured party remedies, collect and realize on the Collateral, consent to use of cash collateral, sell, lease, assign or credit bid the Collateral at public or private sale, purchase at such sale free of redemption rights, and require the Loan Parties to assemble the Collateral; net proceeds are applied to the Obligations in such order as the Agent elects; 10 days' notice of sale is deemed commercially reasonable.

EQUITY CURE: for purposes of determining whether a Default or Event of Default under Section 6.12 has occurred, at any time after the end of a fiscal quarter until the tenth (10th) Business Day after the date financial statements are required to be delivered for that quarter (the 'Cure Expiration Date'), the Company may issue Qualified Stock and apply the net cash proceeds (a 'Specified Equity Contribution') to INCREASE EBITDA for that fiscal quarter, provided the proceeds are actually received as cash common equity by the Cure Expiration Date, are Not Otherwise Applied, and notice is given to the Administrative Agent on receipt (with the designated amount permitted to be reduced to the amount actually needed).
units.notes: The cure operates as an EBITDA add-back, not a debt paydown - see 7.03(b)(iv).

units.description: Equity Cure conditions: (i) no more than two (2) Specified Equity Contributions in any period of four consecutive fiscal quarters; (ii) no more than five (5) in the aggregate during the term of the Agreement; (iii) the amount may not exceed the amount required to achieve pro forma compliance with Section 6.12 for that quarter; (iv) NO pro forma reduction in Indebtedness (including by netting) may be given effect for the cured quarter; (v) Specified Equity Contributions count toward EBITDA ONLY for Section 6.12 compliance and are disregarded for pricing, all other financial-ratio-based conditions (including pro forma tests for basket usage), the Available Amount, and all other purposes; and (vi) once notice of an intent to cure is delivered, no Loans need be made and no Letters of Credit issued, amended or extended until the contribution is made.
units.notes: CRITICAL: condition (v) means a cured quarter does NOT restore basket capacity, pricing benefit or Available Amount build - the cure is ring-fenced to the maintenance covenant only. Two-per-four-quarters and five-lifetime limits.

units.description: Effect of cure: upon receipt of Specified Equity Contribution proceeds before the Cure Expiration Date, Section 6.12 is deemed satisfied for that quarter as though there had been no failure, and any related Default (and any other Default arising solely as a result) is deemed not to have occurred for any Loan Document purpose; and after notice of intent to cure, neither the Administrative Agent nor any Lender may exercise Section 7.02 (or other Loan Document) rights or remedies based solely on a Section 6.12 failure until the failure remains uncured at the Cure Expiration Date.
units.notes: A true standstill: remedies are blocked from the notice of intent through the Cure Expiration Date.

units.description: Standard agency appointment and authorization: irrevocable appointment of JPMorgan as administrative and collateral agent, powers of attorney for non-U.S. Collateral Documents, action only on Required Lender instruction for non-express matters with indemnity/exculpation conditions, purely mechanical and administrative duties with express disclaimer of fiduciary duty (including express exclusion of trustee liability for Canadian-law Collateral), sub-agent appointment, Arranger exculpation, insolvency-proceeding claim-filing authority, and third-party-beneficiary limitation. No independently material content.

Standard Agent exculpation and reliance provisions, including the requirement of express written 'notice of Default' before the Agent is deemed to have knowledge, no duty to inquire into covenant performance, condition satisfaction, Lien perfection or Affiliate Lender compliance, and no duty to monitor Disqualified Institutions. No independently material content.
Approved Electronic Platform posting provisions with 'as is' disclaimers and consequential damages waiver. No independently material content.

The Person serving as Administrative Agent has the same rights and obligations as any other Lender in its individual capacity and may engage in other business with the Loan Parties without accounting. No independently material content.

Agent resignation on 30 days' notice, Required Lender appointment of a successor with Borrower Representative approval (not unreasonably withheld, not required during a continuing Event of Default), and fallback self-appointment by the retiring Agent. No independently material content.

Lender representations that the facility is a commercial lending facility and each Lender made its own credit decision, plus the 2021-vintage erroneous-payment ('Payment Notice') provisions requiring Lenders to return payments made in error within one Business Day with interest and waiving the 'discharge for value' defense. Mechanical, no borrower-facing economic effect.

No Secured Party may individually realize on Collateral or enforce a Guarantee (other than exercising setoff under 9.08 or filing an insolvency proof of claim); all remedies are exercised solely by the Administrative Agent as 'representative' of the Secured Parties. Banking Services and Swap Agreement providers acquire no Collateral management or release rights and are deemed to have appointed the Agent and be bound as Secured Parties. The Agent has no duty to ascertain the existence, value, priority or perfection of Collateral.
units.notes: Materially restricts the rights of hedge and cash-management counterparties despite their sharing in the Collateral at tier four of the 2.18(b) waterfall.

units.description: The Secured Parties irrevocably authorize the Administrative Agent, at Required Lender direction, to credit bid all or any portion of the Secured Obligations at Bankruptcy Code Section 363/1123/1129 sales or other foreclosure sales, form acquisition vehicles, deem ratable assignment of the credit-bid Secured Obligations to those vehicles, issue equity or debt instruments of the vehicles to the Secured Parties ratably, and reassign unused Secured Obligations automatically.

Standard Lender ERISA plan-asset representations and covenants for the benefit of the Agent and Arrangers (not the Loan Parties), tracking PTE 84-14 and related exemptions. No independently material content for the borrower.
JPMorgan's National Flood Insurance Reform Act policy notice and distribution of flood documents to Lenders. No independently material content.
Each Lender appoints the Administrative Agent as fonde de pouvoir/hypothecary representative for purposes of any Quebec deed of hypothec securing Collateral located in Quebec.
units.notes: Necessary to make a Quebec hypothec effective under the Civil Code; a structural piece of the Canadian collateral package.

units.description: Notice addresses for the Borrowers, the Administrative Agent (including the DQ List notification address), the Issuing Bank, the collateral agent and the Lenders; effectiveness rules for hand delivery, courier, fax and electronic delivery, with an exception excluding Article II notices and Section 5.01(c) compliance certificates from default electronic delivery.

Amendments require the Borrowers and Required Lenders, except that: (A) increasing any Lender's Commitment requires that Lender's consent; (B) reducing or forgiving principal, LC Disbursements, interest rate, interest or fees requires each directly affected Lender - but amendments to the FINANCIAL COVENANTS or the defined terms used in them are expressly NOT a reduction in rate or fees; (C) postponing any scheduled payment or Commitment expiration date requires each directly affected Lender (excluding mandatory prepayments under 2.11(c)); (D) altering ratable Commitment reduction or the payment waterfall/sharing (2.09(d), 2.18(b)/(d)) requires each Lender other than Defaulting Lenders and Affiliate Lenders; (E) changing this Section or the 'Required Lenders' definition or any voting threshold requires each directly affected Lender (excluding Defaulting and Affiliate Lenders); (F) changing Section 2.20 requires each Lender; (G) releasing any Guarantor from the Loan Guaranty (except as otherwise permitted) requires each Lender; (H) releasing all or substantially all Collateral (except per 9.02(c) or a Collateral Document) requires each Lender; and (I) changing the 'Alternative Currency' definition requires each Revolving Lender. Agent/Swingline/Issuing Bank consent is required for provisions affecting them; Class-specific amendments may be effected by the affected Class alone.
units.notes: CRITICAL: financial covenant levels (and the defined terms feeding them - EBITDA, Total Net Leverage Ratio, etc.) can be amended by REQUIRED LENDERS only. Guarantee release and all-or-substantially-all Collateral release are sacred rights.

units.description: The Agent is irrevocably authorized in its sole discretion to release Liens (i) upon Payment in Full with satisfactory cash collateralization of Unliquidated Obligations, (ii) on property sold or disposed of where the disposing Loan Party certifies compliance with this Agreement (and where 100% of a Restricted Subsidiary's Equity Interests are sold, to release that Restricted Subsidiary's Loan Guaranty), (iii) on property under expired or terminated leases, and (iv) as required to effect a remedies sale. Otherwise the Agent may not release Liens without Required Lender authorization, except that it may release Liens on Collateral valued in the aggregate at not more than $500,000 per calendar year, and may release Liens in connection with any permitted transaction, relying conclusively on Borrower Representative certificates. The Agent may also subordinate or release Liens in favor of permitted purchase money Lien holders.
units.notes: The $500,000 annual discretionary release allowance and the certificate-reliance mechanic are the practical route by which collateral leaves the package.

units.description: Where Required Lender consent is obtained but a Lender whose consent is also necessary refuses (a 'Non-Consenting Lender'), the Borrowers may replace that Lender by having an acceptable assignee purchase its Loans and Obligations at par, plus payment of accrued interest, fees, Sections 2.15 and 2.17 amounts, and a deemed Section 2.16 break funding amount.

The Administrative Agent may, with the consent of the Borrower Representative ONLY, amend, modify or supplement this Agreement or any Loan Document to cure any ambiguity, omission, mistake, defect or inconsistency.
units.notes: A two-party amendment right without Lender consent - relevant to determining which version of a provision is operative.

units.description: Joint and several expense reimbursement (syndication, administration, amendments, LC issuance, enforcement and workout, with single-counsel-per-jurisdiction limits and conflict exceptions, and Event-of-Default-conditioned appraisal, field examination and collateral protection costs) and a broad joint and several indemnity in favor of Indemnitees covering the Loan Documents, the Transactions, Loans and Letters of Credit, environmental matters, Agent administration and related Proceedings, excluding gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith and disputes solely among Indemnitees. Lenders backstop the Agent Indemnitees ratably. Consequential damages waiver.

Assignment mechanics: consent of the Borrower Representative (deemed given if no objection within ten Business Days; not required for assignments to a Lender, a Lender Affiliate, an Approved Fund, or, during a continuing Event of Default, any assignee), the Administrative Agent, the Issuing Bank and the Swingline Lender, each not unreasonably withheld and each with carve-outs for Term Loan assignments; minimum assignment amounts of $5,000,000 (Revolving) and $1,000,000 (Term) with exceptions; proportionate partial assignments; a $3,500 processing fee; and an Administrative Questionnaire requirement. Assignments to 'Ineligible Institutions' (natural persons, Defaulting Lenders and their Parents, certain personal investment vehicles, Loan Parties/Affiliates except under 9.04(f)/(g), and Disqualified Institutions) are prohibited, and during a continuing Event of Default any non-Lender that would hold more than 25% of Aggregate Revolving Exposure or Commitments is an Ineligible Institution.
units.notes: The 25%-during-default concentration limit and the Disqualified Institution regime are real transfer restrictions with economic effect on who can hold the debt in a workout.

units.description: Customary participation provisions including Participant voting limitations mirroring the 9.02(b) sacred rights, Participant Register maintenance, and yield-protection limitations.

AFFILIATE LENDER ASSIGNMENTS: any Lender may assign Term Loans to an Affiliate Lender (including a Debt Fund Affiliate) only if (A) via a Dutch Auction open pro rata to all Term Lenders of that Class, or an open market purchase on a non-pro-rata basis, per procedures agreed with the Auction Agent; (B) no Event of Default under 7.01(a), (b), (h) or (i) exists or would result; (C) an Affiliate Lender Assignment and Assumption is delivered (Agent need not record for three Business Days); (D) Affiliate Lenders other than Debt Fund Affiliates may not hold Term Loans exceeding 20% of all Term Loans then outstanding (the 'Affiliate Lender Cap'); (E) plan-of-reorganization votes are cast proportionately with non-Affiliate Lenders unless disproportionately adversely treated; (F) status disclosure and voting restrictions; (G) exclusion from Lender-only meetings and information; (H) MNPI representations or disclosure; and (I) Loan proceeds may not fund the assignment. Affiliate Lenders may contribute purchased Term Loans to the Borrowers for cancellation, with pro rata reduction of each amortization installment. Voting: Affiliate Lenders are deemed voted proportionately with non-Affiliate Term Lenders; Debt Fund Affiliates may not exceed 25% of the Required Lender calculation; both retain voting rights on each-Lender or each-affected-Lender matters and on disproportionate or payment-depriving actions.
units.notes: CRITICAL: a 20% sponsor-affiliate holding cap and a 25% Debt Fund Affiliate voting cap materially affect who controls amendments and workouts.

units.description: LOAN BUYBACKS: any Lender may assign Term Loans to the Company, another Borrower or a Restricted Subsidiary only if (A) via a Dutch Auction open pro rata to all Term Lenders of that Class, or an open market purchase on a non-pro-rata basis with all such open market purchases capped at $20,000,000 in the aggregate; (B) no Event of Default exists or would result; (C) purchased Term Loans are automatically and permanently cancelled on acquisition; (D) Loan proceeds may not be used to fund the purchase; (E) outstanding Term Loans and each Section 2.10 amortization installment are reduced pro rata by the par amount purchased; and (F)/(G) MNPI representation or disclosure with Lender acknowledgements.
units.notes: $20,000,000 aggregate cap on non-pro-rata open market buybacks; unlimited via Dutch Auction. Debt bought back must be cancelled, so this is a deleveraging (not a sponsor-hold) construct.

units.description: All covenants, agreements, representations and warranties survive execution and each credit extension regardless of investigation or knowledge of any Default, and continue until Payment in Full; Sections 2.15, 2.16, 2.17 and 9.03 and Article VIII survive repayment and termination indefinitely.

Counterparts, integration (this Agreement, the Loan Documents and separate agency-fee and Issuing Bank Sublimit letter agreements constitute the entire contract), effectiveness, and electronic execution/Electronic Signature provisions.
Standard severability provision.

Upon a continuing Event of Default, each Lender, Issuing Bank and their Affiliates may set off deposits and other obligations owing to any Loan Party against Secured Obligations, whether or not demand has been made and whether or not the obligations are matured; Defaulting Lender setoff proceeds must be turned over to the Administrative Agent for application under Section 2.20.
units.notes: Setoff is one of only two rights a Secured Party may exercise individually notwithstanding Section 8.07.

units.description: The Loan Documents (other than those with a contrary express choice of law) are governed by the internal laws of the STATE OF ILLINOIS, giving effect to federal laws applicable to national banks; claims by Secured Parties against the Administrative Agent are governed by Illinois law notwithstanding any other Loan Document's governing law; with customary jurisdiction, venue and service of process provisions.
units.notes: Illinois (not New York) governing law is unusual for a syndicated facility of this size and is a genuinely distinguishing term.

units.description: Mutual waiver of trial by jury.
Headings and the Table of Contents are for convenience only and do not affect construction.

Confidentiality of 'Information' received from the Borrowers, with nine enumerated permitted disclosures (affiliates and advisors, Governmental Authorities including self-regulatory bodies, legal process, other parties, remedies enforcement, assignees/Participants and swap counterparties subject to equivalent confidentiality - expressly including disclosure of the DQ List, with Borrower Representative consent, rating agencies and the CUSIP Service Bureau, and publicly available or independently obtained information). Includes an MNPI acknowledgement by each Lender.
Lender obligations are several; no Lender is responsible for another's failure; nonreliance acknowledgements; violation of law provisions.
USA PATRIOT Act customer identification notice.
Acknowledgement that Lenders and their Affiliates may have other relationships with the Loan Parties and their Affiliates.

Each Lender appoints each other Lender as agent for perfection by possession or control of Collateral in that Lender's possession, requiring delivery to or dealing at the Administrative Agent's instruction.

Usury savings: if interest plus Charges would exceed the Maximum Rate, the rate is limited to the Maximum Rate and the excess is cumulated and recovered from later periods or other Loans (never above the Maximum Rate) with interest at the Overnight Rate.
units.notes: Paired with the separate Canadian criminal-rate adjustment in Section 2.13(h).

units.description: Arm's-length relationship acknowledgement, no fiduciary or advisory duty, and waiver of fiduciary-duty claims against Credit Parties.
Consent to customary tombstone and marketing use of Loan Party names and transaction details.
EEA/UK bail-in acknowledgement and consent to write-down and conversion powers with respect to liabilities of Affected Financial Institutions.
U.S. special resolution regime (QFC stay) acknowledgements under the FDIA and OLA.
CAML acknowledgement and cooperation obligations for Canadian anti-money-laundering compliance.

Judgment currency provision: conversion into the judgment currency at the rate on the business day before judgment, with the Loan Parties' obligation discharged only to the extent the judgment amount purchases the original currency, and indemnity for any shortfall as a separate obligation.

Each U.S. Loan Guarantor (other than those delivering a separate Guaranty) is jointly and severally liable as primary obligor and unconditionally guarantees to the Secured Parties the prompt payment when due of the Secured Obligations plus Section 9.03 collection costs (the 'U.S. Guaranteed Obligations'), excluding any guarantee of Excluded Swap Obligations; extensions and renewals do not release the guarantor, and the guaranty is enforceable by any branch or Affiliate of any Lender extending part of the obligations.

Each Canadian Loan Guarantor is jointly and severally liable as primary obligor and guarantees only the CANADIAN Secured Obligations plus Section 9.03 collection costs (the 'Canadian Guaranteed Obligations'), excluding Excluded Swap Obligations; and it is expressly provided that notwithstanding anything in this Agreement, NO Canadian Loan Party shall guarantee any U.S. Secured Obligations.
units.notes: CRITICAL entity-applicability: the operative guarantee side of the one-way ring-fence. U.S. Loan Guarantors guarantee the entire Secured Obligations (U.S. and Canadian); Canadian Loan Guarantors guarantee only the Canadian side.

units.description: The Loan Guaranty is a guaranty of payment and not of collection; each Loan Guarantor waives any right to require the Agent, Issuing Bank or Lenders to first sue any Borrower or Obligated Party or to enforce against collateral.

Guarantor obligations are unconditional and absolute and not subject to reduction, limitation, impairment or termination for any reason other than Payment in Full, including waivers or compromises of the Guaranteed Obligations, changes in ownership or structure of any Borrower, insolvency proceedings and resulting releases, or setoff claims; not subject to defenses based on invalidity or unenforceability of the Guaranteed Obligations; and not discharged by failure to enforce, modification, release or non-perfection of security, or delay in payment.

Comprehensive waiver of suretyship defenses, including defenses arising from unenforceability against the Borrower, presentment, demand and protest, any requirement of prior action against an Obligated Party, and any anti-deficiency or election-of-remedies defense arising from judicial or non-judicial foreclosure or deed in lieu.

No Loan Guarantor may assert any subrogation, contribution or indemnification claim against any Obligated Party or collateral until the Loan Parties and Loan Guarantors have fully performed all obligations to the Agent, Issuing Bank and Lenders.

Guarantor obligations are reinstated if any payment of the Guaranteed Obligations is rescinded or restored on insolvency or otherwise; and if acceleration is stayed by an insolvency proceeding, the accelerated amounts are nonetheless payable by the Loan Guarantors on demand.
Each Loan Guarantor assumes responsibility for keeping itself informed of the Borrowers' condition; no duty of the Agent, Issuing Bank or Lenders to advise.

(a) Any Loan Guarantor (other than a Borrower) is AUTOMATICALLY released upon consummation of a transaction permitted by this Agreement as a result of which it ceases to be a Restricted Subsidiary (subject to any required Required Lender consent to that transaction and its terms). (b) The Administrative Agent may, at the Company's request and without Lender consent, release any Loan Guarantor (other than a Borrower) that is NO LONGER A MATERIAL SUBSIDIARY. (c) The Loan Guaranty terminates automatically on Payment in Full of all Secured Obligations.
units.notes: CRITICAL: clause (b) permits guarantor release simply on falling below the 5% EBITDA/asset Material Subsidiary threshold, without Lender consent - a meaningful leakage path from the guarantee package that overrides the 9.02(b)(G) each-Lender consent requirement (which is qualified 'except as otherwise permitted herein').

units.description: Guarantor payments are made free of withholding subject to a gross-up for Indemnified Taxes, mirroring Section 2.17.

Fraudulent-transfer savings clause: each Loan Guarantor's guaranteed amount is limited to the extent necessary so its obligations are not avoidable under Bankruptcy Code Section 548 or any applicable Uniform Fraudulent Transfer/Conveyance or Voidable Transactions Act, taking into account subrogation, indemnification and contribution rights.
units.notes: Directly caps the effective recourse against each guarantor - relevant to any recovery or capacity analysis.

units.description: Contribution regime: a Loan Guarantor making a Guarantor Payment exceeding its 'Allocable Amount' share is entitled, only after indefeasible payment in full and Payment in Full of the Guaranteed Obligations and termination of this Agreement, to contribution and indemnification from the other Loan Guarantors pro rata by Allocable Amount (fair saleable value of property less total liabilities including contingent liabilities).
Each Loan Party's liability as a Loan Guarantor is cumulative with its other liabilities under the Loan Documents, without limitation as to amount.

Each Qualified ECP Guarantor jointly and severally undertakes to provide funds or other support as needed by each other Guarantor to honor its Swap Obligation guarantee obligations, limited to the maximum amount not rendering the undertaking voidable as a fraudulent conveyance; intended to be a 'keepwell, support, or other agreement' under Commodity Exchange Act Section 1a(18)(A)(v)(II) and effective until termination of all Swap Obligations.

The Company is irrevocably appointed by each Borrower as contractual representative ('Borrower Representative') under the Loan Documents and as agent to receive all Loan proceeds in the Funding Account for prompt disbursement to the appropriate Borrower, provided that in the case of a Revolving Loan the amount may not exceed Availability; the Agent and Lenders have no liability for the Borrower Representative's or Borrowers' acts.
units.notes: Because the Company receives and re-disburses all proceeds, intercompany flows must also satisfy Sections 6.01(b) and 6.04(c).

units.description: The Borrower Representative has only the powers specifically delegated plus reasonably incidental powers, with no implied duties.
The Borrower Representative may act through authorized officers.

Each Borrower must immediately notify the Borrower Representative of any Default or Event of Default in a designated 'notice of default'; the Borrower Representative must give prompt notice to the Agent and Lenders; and notice to the Borrower Representative constitutes notice to each Borrower on receipt.
The Borrower Representative may resign with the Agent's prior written consent, effective on appointment of a successor.

The Borrowers empower the Borrower Representative to execute and deliver Loan Documents and related certificates (including Compliance Certificates) on their behalf, and agree that its actions bind all Borrowers.

(a) Each U.S. Borrower is jointly and severally liable for ALL Secured Obligations and is a guarantor of each other Borrower's obligations; each CANADIAN Borrower is jointly and severally liable ONLY for the Canadian Secured Obligations and expressly not for any U.S. Secured Obligations, and guarantees only the other Canadian Borrowers' obligations. (b) Nothing limits any Borrower's direct primary liability for Loans made to or for its benefit, LC Exposure supporting its business, and related interest, fees and expenses.
units.notes: CRITICAL entity-applicability: the borrower-side statement of the one-way ring-fence, parallel to Sections 2.01 and 10.01(b).

units.description: COLLATERAL ALLOCATION MECHANISM: on the CAM Exchange Date - the first date on which either a Section 7.01(h) or (i) insolvency event occurs with respect to any Borrower or the Loans are accelerated under Section 7.02 - (i) the Revolving Commitments terminate automatically, (ii) the principal of each Revolving Loan denominated in an Alternative Currency is automatically converted into Dollars at the Exchange Rate on that date, with all further accruals and payments in Dollars at the rates otherwise applicable, and (iii) the Revolving Lenders are automatically deemed to have made reciprocal purchases of interests in the Designated Obligations so that each Lender owns its CAM Percentage of each Designated Obligation. Each Revolving Lender, each participant and each Borrower consents to the CAM Exchange and agrees to execute confirming notes and documents, though failure to do so does not affect the Exchange's validity or effectiveness.
units.notes: CRITICAL: mutualizes currency and Borrower-specific credit risk among Revolving Lenders on insolvency or acceleration. Note 'Designated Obligations' covers only Revolving Loan principal/interest and commitment fees, so Term Loans, LC Exposure and Swingline Loans are outside the CAM.

units.description: On and after the CAM Exchange Date, every payment received by the Administrative Agent in respect of the Designated Obligations is distributed to the Revolving Lenders pro rata in accordance with their CAM Percentages.
units.notes: Overrides the ordinary ratable-sharing rules for the covered obligations post-CAM.

units.description: Nothing in Article XII prohibits a Revolving Lender from assigning interests in some but not all Designated Obligations after the CAM Exchange, provided the assignor and assignee agree between themselves on their reciprocal rights and obligations in the event of a redetermination of CAM Percentages.
units.notes: FLAGGED AS UNCERTAIN: the clause conditions post-CAM partial assignments on the parties agreeing their rights 'in the event of a redetermination of the CAM Percentages as provided in the immediately preceding paragraph', but paragraph (b) as drafted contains NO CAM Percentage redetermination mechanic (it addresses only pro rata distribution). Whether any redetermination right exists at all, and on what trigger, cannot be determined from this text.

units.description: Following the signature pages the document includes the Commitment Schedule (JPMorgan $40,000,000 revolving / $50,000,000 initial term / $10,000,000 delayed draw / $10,000,000 swingline; Bank of America and CIBC Bank USA $34,000,000 / $42,500,000 / $8,500,000 each; U.S. Bank and TD Bank $19,000,000 / $23,750,000 / $4,750,000 each; totaling $200,000,000 / $250,000,000 / $50,000,000) and form Exhibits A (Assignment and Assumption), B-1 (Borrowing Request), B-2 (Interest Election Request), C-1 through C-4 (U.S. Tax Compliance Certificates), D (Compliance Certificate with Schedules I-III showing detailed Section 6.12 and Applicable Rate calculation tables and the Unrestricted Subsidiary list), E (Joinder Agreement) and F (Affiliate Lender Assignment and Assumption). The disclosure Schedules (1.01, 3.05, 3.06, 3.10(b), 3.13, 3.14, 5.14, 6.01, 6.02, 6.04, 6.05, 6.10) are referenced but NOT reproduced in this filed exhibit.
units.notes: The absence of the disclosure schedules means grandfathered debt, Liens, investments, restrictions, the Effective Date Unrestricted Subsidiary designations and the post-closing obligations cannot be quantified from this document alone.

documentLevelNotes: This is a $500,000,000 cross-border facility ($200,000,000 revolving with a $25,000,000 LC sublimit and a $10,000,000 swingline, a $250,000,000 initial term loan and a $50,000,000 delayed draw term loan), all maturing April 1, 2027, governed by ILLINOIS law (unusual for a facility of this size). The single most distinctive structural feature is a ONE-WAY U.S./CANADIAN RING-FENCE: Canadian Loan Parties never guarantee or secure U.S. Secured Obligations, and this is restated operatively in at least five places (Section 2.01 flush text, 5.13(b) and (e)(i), 6.09(b), 10.01(b) and 11.07(a)); it also drives the affiliate-transaction treatment of U.S.-to-Canada transfers under 6.05(b)(ii). Covenant architecture: two quarterly maintenance covenants (Interest Coverage at 3.00x and Total Net Leverage stepping 4.00x / 3.75x / 3.50x) plus a twice-usable 0.50x Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment holiday triggered by a Material Acquisition (>$75,000,000), and an Equity Cure limited to two per four quarters and five in total whose benefit is expressly ring-fenced to Section 6.12 only. Basket architecture mixes fixed dollar caps with 'greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA' grower baskets and a shared 15%-of-Applicable-EBITDA cap running across 6.01(b)(iii), 6.01(c)(iii) and 6.04(b); a single Available Amount builder is shared between 6.04(q) investments and 6.08(a)(iv) Restricted Payments. Two drafting points a reviewer should flag: (1) Section 6.04(b) states the shared cap as '15% of EBITDA' while the parallel 6.01 provisos say '15% of Applicable EBITDA'; and (2) Section 7.01(o) refers to 'Permitted Liens', which is not a defined term (the defined term is 'Permitted Encumbrances'). Article XII's CAM covers only 'Designated Obligations' (revolving principal, interest and commitment fees), leaving Term Loans, LC Exposure and Swingline Loans outside it, and its clause (c) cross-references a CAM Percentage redetermination mechanic that does not appear in clause (b). Cross-document dependencies: 'Excluded Property' is defined only by reference to the Security Agreements, and the disclosure Schedules (1.01, 3.05, 3.06, 3.10(b), 3.13, 3.14, 5.14, 6.01, 6.02, 6.04, 6.05, 6.10) are referenced but not reproduced in this filed exhibit, so grandfathered debt, Liens, investments, restrictive agreements, the Effective Date Unrestricted Subsidiary list and the Section 5.14 post-closing obligations (breach of which is an immediate no-cure Event of Default) cannot be quantified from this document alone. Finally, note there is NO excess cash flow sweep and no call protection; the only mandatory prepayment triggers are Section 6.05(k) asset sales above a $10,000,000 annual threshold (with a 12/18-month reinvestment right), casualty/condemnation, dispositions of Unrestricted Subsidiaries, and non-permitted debt incurrences - and Term Lenders may decline, with declined amounts feeding back into the Available Amount builder.
